articleTitle: In-Circuit Impedance Measurement Setups of Inductive Coupling Approach: A Review
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In-circuit impedance measurement provides useful information for many EMC applications. The inductive coupling approach is a promising in-circuit impedance measurement method due to its non-contact characteristics and simple on-site implementation. Many measurement setups of this approach were reported. However, a comprehensive survey and comparison of these setups have not been found in the literature. This paper reviews these setups in terms of their characteristics, limitations, and applications. In addition, recommendations for future research are also presented.

articleTitle: Customized Test Fixture for Accurate Impedance Measurement of EMI Filtering Chokes
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Accurate measurement of electromagnetic interference (EMI) filter components provide reliable estimation of filter performance in power electronics applications. This paper proposes a customized test fixture to be used with a vector network analyzer (VNA) for accurate impedance measurement of filtering chokes. By modeling the test fixture as a lumped circuit and de-embedding it from the measurement setup, the true impedance of the choke under test can be obtained with excellent accuracy. The proposed measurement setup with the dedicated test fixture is validated experimentally up to 30 MHz.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Modeling of Induction Motor Using Multilayer Perceptron
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes an easy-to-use accurate high- frequency (HF) behavioral model of induction motor with a simple and straightforward parameterization process for conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) analysis. The HF model contains only six circuit elements per phase with a simple structure and is intended for time-domain simulation of variable frequency drive (VFD) systems. The circuit elements are determined by a multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network, in which only the phase-to-frame impedance is needed for training purposes. Compared with the parameterization methods in conventional motor modeling, the MLP significantly simplifies the parameterization process. Using a three-phase 5.5 kW star-connected induction motor as a case study, the capability and accuracy of the HF model are validated.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of the Induced AC Interference in DC Rails of a Double-Track System
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The article considers a simplified model for evaluating interference in rails induced by a nearby alternating current traction network. The advantage of the proposed simplified model is that the model does not require accurate accounting of the parameters of all track circuits along the entire length of the feeder zone, which greatly simplifies and speeds up the application of the model. The possibility of using such simplification is based on the fact that the track circuits equipment affects the redistribution of the traction return current in two rails, mainly in the local area where this equipment is installed, and this redistribution insignificantly affects the currents in other conductors of traction network, since the distance from rails to other conductors is much greater than the distance between two rails. This assumption allows at the first stage of modeling to determine the distribution of alternating traction current in the conductors of the traction network without taking into account the track circuits equipment. At the second stage of modeling, the equipment of track circuits is taken into account only for the track section for which it is necessary to determine the level of induced interference and evaluate its impact on the operation of track circuits

articleTitle: EMI Modeling for Vehicle Body using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper applies characteristic mode analysis to the vehicle body to better understand the coupling mechanism of the vehicle EMI emission. We discussed a few typical modes of the vehicle body. By visualizing the eigen-current distribution of the vehicle modes, the EMI emission of the vehicle could be suppressed significantly by only putting absorbing material on the local area of the vehicle with relatively high eigen-current intensity. The simulation results show that the characteristic mode analysis method can simplify the electromagnetic analysis process and provide a sufficient theoretical basis for subsequent work.

articleTitle: Surface Electrostatic Discharge Characteristics of Satellite Multilayer Insulation Module
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Multilayer thermal insulation module is mainly coated on the outer surface of spacecraft, which can effectively isolate the external cold and low temperature environment, and is an effective method for spacecraft thermal control design. The simulation results of GEO plasma multilayer insulation module show that the charging and discharging process of multilayer insulation module includes two kinds of effects: surface electrification and internal electrification, while the surface charge discharge effect mainly occurs in the Kapton layer of mask material. In this paper, according to the structural characteristics of the typical flexible secondary surface mirror made of thin film materials, the electron gun is employed to simulate the space charge and discharge environment of GEO satellite. The surface charge potential and discharge pulse of the multilayer insulation module are measured by a noncontact surface potentiometer and the electrostatic discharge monitoring device respectively, Key parameters such as the discharge waveform of the multilayer insulation module material are obtained. The results show that the irradiation electron energy is 25 keV, which is suitable for the simulation test of the space charge discharge effect of the multilayer thin film material, The variation of surface charge potential and radiation electron parameters of multilayer insulation module materials was obtained through the test, which provided effective environmental data and design guidance for the space environment applicability analysis and space application of multilayer insulation module materials.

articleTitle: Insertion Loss Reduction Using Rounded Corners to Mitigate Surface Roughness Effect in PCB Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Signal integrity (SI) can be interpreted as a measure of the distortion of the incident pulse, which is attributed to various contributors, e.g., inter-symbol interference (ISI), crosstalk, jitter, etc. The channel insertion loss is generally the most critical concern in SI designs, since it determines the working bandwidth of a high-speed channel, and the bandlimited channels are known as the root cause of ISI. At the tens of Gigabit rates in use today, PCB transmission lines may have appreciable losses, which can be divided into frequency-dependent dielectric loss and conductor loss, and noticeable amount of losses can be generated at high-frequencies due to the skin effect and copper rough surfaces. In order to reduce the additional conductor loss due to the surface roughness, the employment of low-profile copper foils is a common practice in high-speed digital design. However, this existing method is not cost-effective. In this paper, insertion loss reduction using rounded corners are proposed and verified using both 2D and 3D full-wave simulations for the first time. Rounded corners can mitigate the increased insertion loss due to copper surface roughness in PCB transmission lines, and can be applied in high-speed interconnect designs to increase eye margins. The impact of applying rounded corners on far-end crosstalk is also discussed.

articleTitle: A Comparison of the S-parameter Extrapolation Methods
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This article investigates five s-parameter extrapolation methods, i.e., Polynomial, Polynomial-Logarithmic, Linear, Static, and Zero-padding. The s-parameters extrapolated using these methods, along with the resulted impedance profiles and eye-diagrams are compared. The study reveals three key observations: First, in contrast to the conventional recommendation that s-parameter extrapolation should be avoided, extrapolation can be doable also useful provided the original s-parameter fulfilling certain conditions. Second, the widely adopted Static method and the Zero-padding method (when extrapolation is used) can exhibit less optimal performances in comparison to other extrapolation methods. Third, which extrapolation method to choose is a case by case decision to make. Practitioners need to carefully check the s-parameters before and after extrapolation in order to ensure the meaningful results can be obtained from the extrapolation.

articleTitle: Modeling of Conducted EMI in Motor Drive System Based on Double Pulse Test and Impedance Measurement
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Power electronic devices in high-power motor drive system will generate high-frequency electromagnetic interference (EMI). In this paper, a modeling method of conducted EMI in motor drive system is studied. Based on datasheet and double pulse test, the static and dynamic characteristics of IGBT are obtained, and the behavior model of IGBT is established. The high-frequency impedance model of filter reactor is established by genetic algorithm. The model of induction motor is established by vector fitting method. The conducted EMI circuit model of motor drive system is established on the simulation platform, and the simulated result of model fits well with the measured result.

articleTitle: Bayesian Machine Learning for Extracting Parasitic Parameters of GSG Calibration Standards
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to extract the parasitic parameters of the calibration standards by using the Bayesian optimization algorithm. After several rounds of optimization, the parasitic parameters are optimized so that the calculated value is closest to the full-wave simulation value. The advantage is that only one S-parameter of a known device needs to be used to obtain the parasitic parameters of all calibration standards. Compared with traditional measurement methods, it has the advantages taking less measurement times and coverage of frequency bandwidth. To prove the validity of the technique, the S-parameter of the 4mm microstrip line was simulated as a reference. The extracted parasitic parameters were used in the 16-term error model, the calibration and simulation results are in good agreement up to 100GHz.

articleTitle: Air Vent with Openings of Random Size and Location for Improved EMI Shielding and Air Flow
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Air-vents on a system chassis are designed to allow efficient air flow to cool the system, while at the same time shield unwanted electromagnetic energy. This paper investigated the air vent with openings of random size and location for better shielding effectiveness (SE) and air resistance performance. Dozens of cases were simulated and demonstrate that there exist some random cases which have better SE in certain frequency range and/or air resistance performance.

articleTitle: Study on Capability Verification Test of Electromagnetic Pulse Protection for Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In order to meet the needs of aviation equipment in the complex electromagnetic environment of battlefield in the future, a typical electromagnetic pulse (EMP) environment is built by the EMP simulation equipment and general simulation equipment.The strong electromagnetic pulse effect test of typical equipment, structure, cable, aperture and whole plane is carried out, the electromagnetic protection capability of military aircraft is verified from three levels: equipment level, cabin level and whole plane level. Through combing and evaluating the test flow, the test section and test type are constructed, and the test method of military aircraft protection verification under strong electromagnetic pulse is summarized by applicability study.

articleTitle: Investigation of Conducted Electromagnetic Interference of Three-Level SiC Power Module
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a 1200-V/200-A three-level silicon carbide (SiC) power module with neutral point clamped (NPC) topology has been investigated in terms of electromagnetic interference (EMI). Compared with traditional two-level SiC modules, the three-level module can effectively alleviate voltage stress of the device, and ensure lower spectrum amplitude of the output terminal voltage below resonance frequency. However, the three-level module presents higher spectrum amplitude in high-frequency (HF) ranges (above 10 MHz) due to the aggravated switching ringings. As a result, RC snubber circuit is required to mitigate such ringings and reduce spectrum amplitude for three-level module. According to relative experimental results, it can be figured out that the three-level NPC power module combined with RC snubber circuit can suppress switching ringings, which is critical for reducing the level of conducted EMI.

articleTitle: Signal Integrity with Ultra-Low Latency in Heterogeneous Integration System in Display (HiSID)
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Heterogeneous Integrated System in Display (HiSID) is a novel display architecture we proposed, in this scenario, screens, components or even the mainboard could be integrated into one module. Beyond the display, components such as computing units, storage units, interaction units and communication units can be combined with the display and then lead to a diverse functionality for the future terminal devices. Physically, this paradigm benefits from the highly-packed structure. But more importantly, according to our simulations, the key transmission path in HiSID would decrease by 80%, which then facilitate the increase of transmission speed by 5 times. To gain a holistic picture, we also systemically discussed the possible challenges for signal integrity, such as the tendency of signal crosstalk, insufficient materials resistivity and unideal thermal management design. Based on our study and discussions, we envision that, the signal integrity with ultra-low latency would enable HiSID with multiple applications.

articleTitle: Measurement-based Modeling of High Frequency Equivalent Circuit of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor of Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The high-frequency circuit model of drive motor will affect the accuracy of electromagnetic interference (EMI) prediction of electric drive system. Therefore, a measurement-based high-frequency equivalent circuit modeling method for the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) of electric vehicles (EVs) is proposed. The common mode (CM) and differential mode (DM) impedance of star-connected PMSM is measured using a vector network analyzer (VNA). According to resonance points on the impedance curve, the circuit topology of motor winding is determined and parameters are calculated, the high-frequency CM and DM equivalent circuit models of PMSM are established respectively. There is a clear correlation between the components and geometry of the motor. The simulation and measurement comparison results verify the accuracy of the model. The influence of the motor impedance on the conducted EMI is analyzed through the system conducted emission test. Using this model, main components of PMSM that cause conducted emission to exceed the standard can be found, which provides a theoretical basis for suppressing conducted EMI exceeding the standard point.

articleTitle: A method to determine an electrical parameter of form-in-place shielding material with two other parameters known by calculation and simulation
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: These years, the form-in-place electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials are more widely used in manufacture of radio base stations for its excellent performance in forming and automatic fabricating. These materials contain different particles in silicone elastomer which bring a challenge to construct model for evaluating its shielding effectiveness when simulating. Three electrical parameters, however, should be already known for accurate modeling. This paper provides a method to determine the third parameter with identified two other parameters. Firstly, a fixture with cavity to cavity has been used to measure the scattering parameter, which is also been modeled in the electromagnetic simulation software with or without shielding material. Then, the relationship between three electrical parameters (conductivity, permeability, permittivity) and shielding effectiveness has been modeled. The shielding effectiveness of the materials can be derived by the difference of scattering parameters S21 measured or simulated with and without shielding materials. Subsequently, the third electrical parameter can be calculated by the relationship established. Eventually, three electrical parameters are used to simulate in the software and result demonstrates that simulation and test maintain good consistency.

articleTitle: The Analysis and Suppression of Electromagnetic Interference on Satellite Automatic Identification System
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In satellite, the layout of the equipment is as possible as compact to reduce the cabin space. As a result, the electronic equipment, antennas, and cables are getting very close， causing the serious electromagnetic interference (EMI) issue. This paper investigates the mechanism of EMI between the automatic identification system (AIS) and the star sensor. A method is proposed to determine the noise interference source and the noise coupling path. The techniques to decrease the EMI due to the radiation coupling are developed. Experiments are conducted to validate the analysis and the proposed techniques.

articleTitle: EMI Source Positioning by Phase Inversion and Near-Field Scanning
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a phase inversion method based on near-field scanning is proposed, which can be used for the positioning of the unknown electromagnetic interference (EMI) source. First, the radiated near field from an unknown source is obtained by the near-field scanning. Then, based on the near-field phase, equivalent dipoles are employed as inversion sources. By exciting all inversion sources in the inversion problem, a strong superposition of field at the original unknown source point can be found, which indicates the location of original source. Both numerical and measurement examples are used to validate the proposed method, which shows a good accuracy in the EMI source positioning.

articleTitle: Discussion on Computing Isotropy of E-field Probe
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A discussion on computing isotropy of E-field probe is proposed. The current isotropic computation in IEEE-1309 is based on geometric mean, which is actually a mathematical algorithm but lack of physical meaning. This paper proposed a new algorithm on computing isotropy of E-field probe based on the concept of power density, which has more physical meaning and more reasonable for logic of isotropy. The new algorithm then compared to the current one in IEEE-1309. The results show that the difference is about 0.47dB in worst case, which is relatively large. But the new algorithm is more comprehensive as using data in every measurement position instead of using maximum and minimum value only.

articleTitle: Calculation and Assessment for HEMP Response of Overhead Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The high altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) generates induced voltage and current with high amplitudes and very steep front edges on transmission lines. The frequency domain chain parameter matrix method was adopted to model the HEMP responses of overhead transmission lines, the induced voltage and current of HEMP responses are calculated for the transmission lines with different voltage levels in combination with the impact characteristics of incident angle, ground conductivity and line length, and the HEMP impact on the overhead transmission lines are assessed. These could provide the basic data for developing protection measures for power grid.

articleTitle: A Single-fed Circularly-Polarized UHF Yagi-Uda Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a wide band circularly polarized Yagi-Uda antenna is proposed. The design consists of two orthogonal linear polarized Yagi antennas and two coupling rods The main advantage of this design is that it not only has a very high gain but also realize circular polarization, thus it could be an excellent candidate for satellite communication. To verify the proposed design, both simulations and measurements are conducted. The results show that the antenna realize a S11 < -10 dB bandwidth 360 MHz to 454 and an axial ratio (AR) < 3 dB bandwidth from 374 MHz to 424 MHz, with a maximum gain of 9.3 dBi.

articleTitle: Switchable Optically Transparent Frequency Selective Surface for ultrawide-band Electromagnetic Shielding
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: An optically transparent frequency selective surface (FSS) for broadband electromagnetic shielding is proposed in this paper. The proposed FSS consists of a polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) layer sandwiched between two Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) layers. The Ω-shape pattern is engraved on PDMS to form the microfluidic channels, where a liquid metal flows through. The electromagnetic response of the proposed design can be switched from all-pass to bandstop characteristic by injecting a liquid metal such as eutectic gallium indium (EGaIn) into the microchannels. Simulated results demonstrate that the 18.8 GHz bandwidth of SE ≥ 10 dB is achieved, with angular stability up to 80° for both TE and TM modes. Meanwhile, the transparency of the proposed shield can reach up to 81%.

articleTitle: A Pilot Test for Radiation Electric Field of ±200kV Hybrid DC Breaker in Short Circuit Fault
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In the case of short-circuit fault, the DC converter station of VSC-HVDC would produce transient electromagnetic field, which would interfere and impact on the secondary equipment in the converter station. This paper analyzes transient electromagnetic field in the short circuit tests of the VSC-HVDC system in a converter station. The time and frequency characteristics of the electric field signals in the DC valve hall have been discussed. For the measurement probe near the hybrid DC breaker, the highest amplitude measured between the two hybrid breakers is 5.1 kV/m while the most frequency components are below the 1 MHz. These transient electric field signal has potential application in the monitoring and diagnosis the states of the DC breaker.

articleTitle: Surface Mounted Parallel Coupled Microstrip Bandpass Filter With Vertical Transition for 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A parallel-coupled microstrip bandpass filter (BPF) for the fifth-generation (5G) millimeter-wave (mm-wave) base station is presented with a novel vertical transition for surface mounting. The vertical transition of side layer connection is applied to surface mounting technology (SMT). A simplified equivalent circuit model is introduced by theoretical analysis to prove the feasibility of the side layer connection structure. The proposed BPF is fabricated by 99.9% Al2O3 substrate with a compact dimension of 9 mm × 6 mm × 0.25 mm. The frequency response of proposed BPF is centered at 28 GHz with a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of more than 14%, a low insertion loss less than 1.5 dB and two transmission zeros near the passband edges. Both measured and simulated results suggest that the proposed BPF is a possible candidate for the application of base station at 5G mm-wave frequencies.

articleTitle: EMI Source Positioning Method Based on Phaseless Near-field Scanning
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an EMI source positioning method based on differential evolution (DE) algorithm is proposed. The location of unknown electromagnetic interference (EMI) source in the shielding box is calculated by phaseless near-field. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by two simulation examples.

articleTitle: An Accurate Time-Domain Simulation Technique for High-Power Electromagnetic Environments
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the propagation of several high-power electromagnetic (HPEM) environments are simulated in free space through finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods based on face-centered cubic (FCC) grids. Three typical HPEM environments including ultra wide band (UWB), high-altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) and high-power microwave (HP-M), are analyzed. Comparing the calculated results of the FCC-FDTD method with the analytical results, or with the FDTD methods with smaller grid in three numerical examples, the FCC-FDTD method is proved to be an effective and stability method to simulate HPEM environments.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Analysis of Microstrip Lines Terminated with Complex Circuits via Time Domain Modeling Method
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: An novel time-domain hybrid method, proposed by integrating transmission line (TL) equations, finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, Substitution theorem, Norton’s theorem and NGSPICE software, is proposed for the crosstalk analysis of microstrip lines (MSLs) terminated with complex circuits. Firstly, the overall structure of microstrip lines is decomposed into a cascade network of multiple microstrip lines and complex circuits. Secondly, the TL equations combined with the FDTD is employed to solve the voltage and current responses on these MSLs, and the effects of these MSLs on the connecting nodes are equivalent to Norton’s circuits according to the Norton’s theorem, which are incorporated into the complex circuits to form new circuit subsystems. Then, the NGSPICE software is applied for the conducted interference analysis of these circuit subsystems to solve the voltage responses on these complex circuits at each time step of FDTD simulation. Finally, the port voltages of these complex circuits are fed back to the MSLs as boundary conditions, which can obtain the effects of complex circuits to these MSLs based on the Substitution theorem. By numerical simulation of three microstrip lines terminated with one complex circuit excited by lumped voltage source, the correctness of this proposed method has been verified by comparing with that of commercial simulation software CST.

articleTitle: Biological experimental study on cumulative effect of vehicle electromagnetic radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: compared with power frequency magnetic field or mobile phone, electric vehicles are equipped with more and more high-voltage components, more and more electronic components, and their frequency, waveform and modulation mode are more flexible, which may make the electromagnetic exposure scene of passengers in the vehicle more complex. With the acceleration of the comprehensive electrification trend of public transport, people are exposed to electric vehicles more and more frequently, and the time is also gradually increasing. Whether the cumulative effect of vehicle electromagnetic radiation has an impact on occupant health is a matter of general concern to consumers. At present, there is still a lack of relevant research and standards on the cumulative effect of vehicle electromagnetic radiation at home and abroad. In this paper, a pure electric vehicle is taken as the test object, and the test mice are taken as an example to verify whether the cumulative effect of vehicle electromagnetic radiation has an impact on the body weight and blood immune cells of mice. The results showed that there were significant gender differences in body weight. However, the test time needs to be further increased to judge whether the cumulative effect causes the impact.

Author Keywords: cumulative effects of vehicle electromagnetic radiation

articleTitle: Inductively Coupled In-Circuit Impedance Measurement Under Low Signal-to-Noise Ratio
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The in-circuit impedance stands as a key factor for assessing the operating status and health condition of electrical assets. The inductive coupling approach is an effective way of measuring the in-circuit impedance of an electrical system due to its non-contact nature and simplicity of on-site implementation. This paper investigates the impact of low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions on the measurement accuracy using the recently developed single-probe measurement setup of the inductive coupling approach. Further this study suggests an effective way to improve measurement accuracy under low SNR conditions.

articleTitle: Comparison Study on EMI Performance of SiC and Si diodes in Cockcroft-Walton Voltage Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This work studies the electromagnetic interference (EMI) performance of Silicon Carbide (SiC) Schottky barrier diode in the Cockcroft-Walton voltage multiplier (CWVM). It’s compared with Silicon (Si) fast recovery diode based on the time-domain waveforms and frequency-domain spectra. The experimental result shows that the EMI in SiC-based CWVM is more severe than the Si-based from frequency over 300 kHz. However, with stage numbers of CWVM increased to 6, EMI levels of both circuits are similar.

articleTitle: Analysis of Neural Spike Signal Transmission Characteristics in 3-D Heterogeneous Integration
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: With the continuous development of artificial intelligence, spiking neuromorphic chip is favored for its architectural advantages of memory computing integration. The neural spike signal is used as the transmission signal in the spiking neuromorphic chip, and its completely different characteristics from the digital pulse signal will inevitably lead to different signal integrity problems. In this paper, we model the common Through Silicon Via (TSV) and the interconnection structure model of redistribution layers (RDL) in 3-D heterogeneous integration, analyze the insertion loss and transient impedance of the two structures respectively, and finally perform time-domain transient simulations with neural spike signals of different rising edges in the two models to observe their transmission characteristics. The simulation results show that neural spike signals with shorter rising edges can generate more serious signal integrity problems such as loss, reflection, and delay in the RDL-TSV interconnection structure.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of EMI Filter Considering the Components Frequency Variation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The EMI filter usually is designed based on the nominal value of filter components such as capacitor and inductor. However, the impedance of these components vary widely in different filtering frequency band, so that the insertion loss of the actual EMI filter may be much lower than its design data in the high frequency span. To improve the EMI filter performance in high frequency, an optimized method considering the frequency variation characteristics of components is proposed. The filter components frequency variation models are established with a frequency response analyzer. Based on these frequency variation models, the actual EMI filter insertion loss is calculated by the cascaded parameters and compared with the required value. The EMI filter can be optimized by comparing the calculation results of different filters. The EMI measurement in an inverter proved the validity of the EMI filter optimized method.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of Nearby Lightning Pulse Magnetic Field Generator
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Nearby lightning pulse magnetic field can cause interference even damage to electronic information equipment and magnetic sensitive elements in navigation device. In order to research on the influence of different design parameters on the internal magnetic field of the pulse magnetic field generator, the double current loop structure with different current loop radius, different section radius and different connection modes are simulated by CST. The simulation results show that when the injection current is the same, the larger the radius of the current loop, the smaller the magnetic induction intensity in the loop; when the radius of the current loop is the same, the section radius has little effect on the magnetic field in the loop area; the magnetic field distribution in parallel loop structure is better than that in series loop structure. The simulation results can provide reference for the design of nearby lightning pulse magnetic field generator.

articleTitle: EM Environment Adaptability Evaluation of Ultrashort Wave Frequency Hopping Radio based on Exploratory Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic environment adaptability is one of the important factors that restrict the effectiveness of equipment. In the process of equipment development, it plays a great role in improving the electromagnetic environment adaptability of equipment to consider the targeted design and evaluation from the top-level design stage. In this paper, the exploratory data analysis method is introduced into the relevant evaluation. Taking ultrashort wave frequency hopping radio as an example, the exploratory data analysis is carried out on the typical factors affecting the adaptability, such as channel interference rate, interference signal ratio, frequency accuracy and interference suppression time. By computation, the influence order of each factor on the adaptability is obtained, which provides a strong data support for the top-level design of equipment.

articleTitle: Water calorimeter design and correction factor analysis for RF medium power measurement
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A water calorimeter is designed based on water for RF medium power measurement by National Institute of Metrology (NIM), based on water calorimetric method. Calorimeter system is designed with measurement capability of 1 W-100 W in power and 10 MHz-7.5 GHz in frequency. Since power range is as wide as 1 W-100 W, severe fluctuation occurs in thermopile output results, caused by temperature change in water bath, power sensor and laboratory ambient. Hence measurement is divided into two scenarios: 1 W -10 W and 10 W – 100 W, where heat exchange of water bath is turned off/on. Correction algorithm is schemed out using reference thermopile and PT100 platinum resistance thermometer, aiming to eliminate both fast and slow variation of calorimetric results. Corrected thermopile results show much more satisfying stability, with relative standard deviation decreased from 3% to 1% approximately. Measurement stability and repeatability are less than 0.6% and 0.5% in AC condition, in terms of relative standard deviation. Measurement in RF condition agrees with monitor RF power sensor well, with relative error less than 0.4%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Antenna Interference by using Antenna Near-Field Directivity
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the difference of radiation directivity between near and far-fields of antennas is introduced. Even if its far-field pattern is omnidirectional, there is a high probability that the near-field pattern of an antenna has a strong directivity. The accuracy of near-field directivity simulation is verified by comparing tests of a Wi-Fi antenna. A practical antenna interference scenario is simulated, showing that the omnidirectional antenna has a strong near-field directivity, and it also matches the test results. If the near-field directivity of the omnidirectional antenna is analyzed in product R&D, the maximum isolation benefit can be more than 20 dB. Finally, this paper introduces a case of using simulation to analyze the antenna near-field directivity and effectively solving the interference problem.

articleTitle: The Research on Frequency-Domain Characteristics of Electromagnetic Pulse
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, Frequency-Domain characteristics of three different sets of High-altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) are calculated by Fourier transform. Results prove that the frequency spectrum characteristics, normalization cumulative power energy and power energy spectrum density are relationship with the HEMP waveform parameter. It is possible to be helpful to the HEMP coupling research and the HEMP protection techniques research. Furthermore, the result can be used to expand HEMP generator application in the civil system by changing HEMP waveform parameters. It is possible to use the results to model high-power electromagnetic devices that is non-standard and has short pulse duration.

articleTitle: Conducted EMI Analysis and Modeling for the Main Circuit of a MMC Submodule
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) has been a nonignorable problem in modular multilevel converter(MMC) systems. Especially inside the submodules, severe EMI excited by the main circuit can be easily coupled to auxiliary circuits and affects their normal operation. In this paper, the conducted EMI of a MMC submodule is studied and modeled using time-domain simulation, based on interference source modeling and distributed parameter extraction. Then no-load test and double-pulse test are applied to verify the proposed model.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis for Electromagnetic Emission Characteristics of Electric Vehicles Based on MATLAB App Designer
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Aiming at the electromagnetic interference characteristics of electric vehicles, a simulation analysis software of electromagnetic emission characteristics is designed and developed by using MATLAB App Designer. The software not only realizes the separation of the modeling of vehicle coupling path and the interference source/sensitive equipment characteristics, but also achieves the simulation prediction under the coexistence of multiple interference sources/sensitive equipment. The software is applied to the electromagnetic coupling simulation between in vehicle systems and the electromagnetic radiation emission prediction of high-voltage system outside the vehicle under the real vehicle state; The software has the characteristics of convenient operation and rapid iteration, which can shorten the vehicle development cycle and reduce the development cost.

articleTitle: The Numerical Analysis of the Doppler Effect of an Arbitrarily Shaped PEC Object in Uniform Motion
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In the paper, a novel numerical method in the frequency domain of analyzing the Doppler effect of an arbitrarily shaped PEC object in uniform motion is proposed. The frame hopping technique and electric integral equation method are used to get the spectrum of the scattering field. After changing the order of operators on the surface current of the PEC object, no Fourier transformation need to be implemented to get the spectrum of the scattering field in the frame at rest with respect to the observer which makes the method efficient.

articleTitle: Prediction of Cavity IEMP Responses in Satellites by using a 3D Parallel Full Electromagnetic PIC Method
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: System generated electromagnetic pulse (SGEMP) that is generated in cavities, known as cavity IEMP (Internal Electromagnetic Pulse), would damage the sensitive electronic devices inside satellites, thus affecting their survival. To investigate the intensity of the cavity IEMP in satellites, a 3D parallel full electromagnetic Particle-in-Cell (PIC) method is introduced, which has the ability to solve problems with hundred millions 3D structured cells and hundred millions macroparticles in a supercomputer. It is then applied to predict the cavity IEMP responses in a satellite exposed to transient X-rays. Results indicate that a very harsh electromagnetic environment is formed inside satellites due to radiation of X-rays, which suggests that a proper radiation harden design should be taken to protect the sensitive electronics against the cavity IEMP inside satellites.

articleTitle: Research on Transient Conduction Sensitivity of the Chips Using TLP Method
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The response characteristics of six integrated circuits subjected to pulse conducted interference are investigated by TLP test method. The three loops from chips under test are selected to suffer pulse conducted interference, including VCC to ground, input to ground and output to ground. Results are summarized and compared by type of chips. Some interesting phenomena are discovered and analyzed in this paper.

articleTitle: Fixture Design for Parasitic Capacitances of MOSFETs for EMI Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Due to the fast-switching nature of modern power converters, up to hundreds of MHz of common-mode noise can easily be generated. The characterization of switching components, e.g., Si MOSFETs, is essential for noise reduction. However, limited by the bandwidth of instruments, the voltage-dependent capacitances of high voltage MOSFETs are typically characterized at approximately 1 MHz, which is insufficient for EMI applications. In this paper, the measurement method and the test fixtures are presented. The measurement bandwidth is pushed to 30 MHz and higher, and frequency-dependent capacitances of a MOSFET are observed through measurements.

articleTitle: Vehicle electromagnetic interference suppression using characteristic mode analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposed to suppress the vehicle electromagnetic interference (EMI) emission by exploring the characteristic mode analysis (CMA) on the vehicle body. We calculated the characteristic modes of the vehicle body and eigen-current using the CMA method. The optimal position range of the DC/DC module, where the EMI emission could be suppressing significantly, could be obtained based on the characteristic modes and eigen-currents. Simulation results show the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed method for vehicle EMI mitigation.

articleTitle: A Lens Antenna Design for In-Cabin Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave (MMW) lens antenna for cabin detection with an operating bandwidth of 60 GHz to 64 GHz. Based on the principle of path compensation, the beam of the antenna can be adjusted by loading a lens above the antenna. This can make the antenna gain of different angles in the cabin balanced, which can increase the stability of in-cabin people detection, especially the stability of multi-people detection. At the same time, it attenuates the reflection of the target outside the cabin and reduces the interference. Simulation results show that the method can achieve beam adjustment within a beamwidth of ±50°.

articleTitle: Quantitative Representation of Frequency Dispersion of Primary Parameters of Shielded-FPC
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to quantitatively express the frequency dispersion of primary parameters of flexible printed circuits with a thin conductive shield. Unlike basic transmission lines, the physical phenomenon of theses frequency dispersion characteristics has not been completely clarified and cannot be predicted quantitatively. The quantitative representation would be an important design guide for implementing conductive shields on the transmission lines. This paper provides a quantitative representation method of the frequency dispersion by fitting mathematical expression. It is demonstrated that the frequency dispersion of resistance and inductance caused by implementing the thin conductive shield can be expressed quantitatively as sigmoid functions.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Traveling-Wave Slot Array for X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, based on a single-ridged waveguide (SRWG) and a rectangular waveguide (RWG), a 16 ×56 slotted waveguide antenna array with dual-polarization, high gain and low side-lobe level is designed and simulated at X-band to validate the slot antenna design for the traveling wave. In this array, the longitudinal slot etched on the broad sidewall of the SRWG is employed for vertical polarization (VP) radiation, while the inclined slot cut in the narrow wall of the RWG is employed for horizontal polarization (HP) radiation. From the simulated results, the bandwidth of the designed antenna for voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) < 1.5 is 0.8GHz at the center frequency of 9.4 GHz. The realized gain at 9.4 GHz is 31dBi with antenna efficiencies better than 83%. The side-lobe level is controlled lower than -31dB over the entire bandwidth. The beam width is 1.6 degrees and the beam direction is 4.5 degrees at 9.4 GHz. The realized gain, beam width, beam pointing and side-lobe of the two polarization modes are almost the same at 9.0GHz, 9.4 GHz and 9.8 GHz. Due to its high gain, compact size, low side-lobe level and easy manufacturing, this array can be combined with the edge-slotted waveguide array to build a two-dimensional dual-polarization antenna array for the applications of sea based X-band radar, satellite communication station, etc.

articleTitle: A Study on ESD Protection Characteristic Difference Measurement of Varistors by VNA
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The protection performance of an electrostatic-discharge (ESD) protection device changes when the device is implemented in a circuit at a system level. Additionally, the operating characteristics and protection performance of an ESD-protection device may differ from device to device even if the specifications of both devices are identical. Therefore, this study aims to realize an evaluation method that can express realistic differences in the ESD-protection performance of devices relying on variable resistor (Varistor). First, we evaluated the application of the proposed method to measurement of the protection characteristics of varistors using a vector network analyzer. Second, we measured and compared three types of varistors that have identical electrical specifications. We present the measured results for the frequency responses of the identical varistors in their operating and non-operating states. The results showed that our proposed method had a possibility to be applied to a realistic evaluation of varistors.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic interference characteristics of vehicle-mounted high-voltage electric drive system
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper analyzes the electromagnetic interference (EMI) source of the electric drive system and its propagation path, theoretically analyzes the electromagnetic interference factors of its output characteristics, and designs and builds a test platform for the high-voltage three-phase line conducted EMI of the electric drive system under complicated working conditions., Studied the influence of factors such as the torque and speed of the motor on the conducted EMI of the high-voltage three-phase line, and provided a theoretical basis for improving the electromagnetic compatibility of the electric drive system of electric vehicles in my country.

articleTitle: A U-shape Compensation Structure for Differential-to-Common Mode Conversion Noise Suppression in 90°-Bended differential Line
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: a U-shaped structure, based on the equivalent lumped circuit of differential transmission line, is proposed to suppress the noise of differential-common-mode conversion. With the equivalent lumped circuit, the cause of mode conversion noise is analyzed. The U-shaped structure has reached the suppression level of 24.31 dB from DC to 10 GHz according to the simulated result.

articleTitle: Proficiency Testing Scheme of Conducted disturbance at telecommunication ports
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The paper introduces a proficiency testing scheme of conducted disturbance at telecommunication ports, includes the items, homogeneity, stability, statistical analysis, result evaluation and unacceptable reason analysis. Through this scheme, we understand the ability of participants to carry out conducted disturbance test at telecommunications ports, find the problems and help them improve their testing capabilities.

articleTitle: A Simple Method for Extracting Complex Permeability of Magnetic Core in Common-Mode Choke
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In the design of Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Filter, the frequency-dependent complex permeability plays an important role for the high frequency performance of the common-mode choke. In this paper, based on the admittance measurement and three-dimensional (3-D) electromagnetic simulation, a method is proposed to extract the complex permeability of magnetic core by considering the effect of dielectric loss, parasitic capacitance and magnetic loss. The 3-D electromagnetic models of single coil and common-mode choke were established respectively by fitting the extracted results. The proposed extraction method was validated by the good agreement between the measured and the simulated results.

articleTitle: Accurate Simulation Methodology of RSE (Radiated Spurious Emission) on Electronic Device
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a method of simulating the non-linear behavior on electronic device, aiming at studying the typical RSE (radiated spurious emission) problems due to non-linear characteristic of electrical connection. The non-linear behavior on a metal-metal contact could be influenced by many factors, such as contact metal types, pressure, fundamental power and aging effects. We propose a RSE simulation workflow and analyzed the factors of nonlinear behavior using the clip and foam gasket. Furthermore, we find the good correlation of simulation and measurement results, confirming the validity of this method.

articleTitle: An FSS-Based Broadband Absorber for Electromagnetic Shielding
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A broadband absorber based on frequency selective surface (FSS) for electromagnetic shielding is proposed in this paper. The proposed absorber consists of a lossy FSS layer and a ground-backed Polymethylacrylimide (PMI) Foam. The lossy FSS layer composes of a square ring and a meandered square spiral made of indium tin oxide (ITO), which is a resistive material with square resistance of 15 Ω/sq. Results show that the proposed absorber achieves more than 90% absorption in the frequency range of 7.4 - 18.7 GHz, with angular incidence stability up to 35° for both TE and TM polarizations.

articleTitle: 2-Port GSG Probe Calibration Using TRL and 16-Term Error Model Up to 100GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper introduces two calibration methods— Thru-Reflect-Line (TRL) and 16-term error model—and explores the influence of crosstalk errors of different intensities on the calibration accuracy of the two methods through full-wave simulation. The 2-port network is calibrated up to 100GHz by TRL and 16-term error model respectively through the GSG probe and calibration standards. When there is strong crosstalk between the two ports, the calibration accuracy of TRL will be deteriorated, while using the 16-term error model for calibration can effectively improve the calibration accuracy when there is a strong crosstalk error. When the crosstalk intensity is small, the accuracy of the 16-term error model is also slightly higher than that of TRL.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Susceptibility of Capacitive Touchscreens to External Electric Field Interference
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Since the introduction of the iPhone, the touchscreen has become one of the most important human-machine interfaces between users and electronic products. The capacitive touch screen is the most popular touchscreen on the market because of its benefits over a resistive touchscreen. However, since the capacitive touchscreen senses the finger-touch by sensing the capacitance change, it is subjected to the interference of the external electric field, which results in touchscreen malfunction and security issues. This paper will first analyze the working principle of the capacitive touchscreen. The mechanism of false (ghost) touch due to external electric field is explored based on the working principle. The conditions of false touch due to the external electric field will be identified and studied. Experiments are conducted to validate and quantify the analysis above. Different from existing literature, which mostly focuses on demonstrating the results without fully understanding the detail mechanism, this paper focuses on disclosing the fundamentals and identifying critical conditions behind the ghost touch phenomena, which is the major contribution of this paper.

articleTitle: Fast Calculation and Optimization of Dense Signal/Ground Vias in System-in-Package
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic leakage from dense signal/ground vias is calculated by integral technologies including contour integral method, surface equivalence theorem and radiated field integral equation, and verified by full-wave simulation software CST Studio Suite. The proposed technologies have a significant time reduction, and the calculated results agree well with the full-wave simulation ones. The radiated power of signal/ground via arrays is further analyzed, and the reason why various signal/ground via distributions result in different radiated emission levels is analyzed. As a result, this paper provides a guide for the arrangement of dense signal/ground vias in system-in-package.

articleTitle: Research on applicability of "full coverage method" in GB 34660 same type determination on high-voltage system of electric vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Electric vehicle(EV) has a variety of high-voltage(HV) system configurations. To reduce testing cost, "full coverage method" is proposed in "GB 34660 same type determination technical requirements". In this paper, the applicability of this method is analyzed by measuring common mode current and radiation with five HV system configurations. The preliminary results suggest that every configuration of HV system should be tested for accurate test result.

articleTitle: Research on Application of Lightning Indirect Effect Test in Automotive Field
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In order to ensure the safety of vehicles in the lightning and lightning environment, related research is carried out on the lightning test in the automotive field. By analyzing the location and waveform characteristics of lightning effects and the coupling mechanism that affects the safety driving of vehicles, test method of indirect lightning effects based on small current extrapolation is proposed. It has been verified by experiments that the method can effectively evaluate the anti-lightning performance of automotive products, and is helpful to provide references for the formulation of relevant standards, business promotion, and vehicle development and design.

articleTitle: Time series modeling and prediction of wideband electric field radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Exposure to wideband electromagnetic radiation (EMR) over seven days was measured in this paper, and a short-time Fourier transform analysis on this showed that the change of EMR over time conforms to people’s daily work and rest cycle and is affected by the intensive use of wireless communication devices, thus showing strong low-frequency periodicity and high-frequency fluctuations. These characteristics lead to a significant decrease in the performance of traditional EMR time series mod-els. To this end, a hybrid model based on wavelet decomposition (WD) and long-short time memory (LSTM) is proposed for the wideband electric field radiation prediction. The proposed model is verified by the measurement samples under different prediction steps. It is also compared with other representative models, and the results show that the proposed model outperforms other models in prediction accuracy and prediction steps.

articleTitle: A Wideband Absorber for Decoupling of Wideband End-fire MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a low profile wideband absorbers based on capacitive surface is proposed, to absorb the interference electromagnetic radiation of a 2-element MIMO array consisting of two half-dimensional Vivaldi antennas placed on a metal surface. Low profile and wideband absorbers are placed between the two units to reduce coupling between the units. The absorbers, with 102.9% absorption bandwidth and good absorption. The Vivaldi antenna is placed on a metal surface, with 99.8%(2.33GHz-7GHz) of the working bandwidth. The isolation between half Vivaldi antenna elements is below 20dB without absorbers, under the action of the absorbers, the isolation of the two semi-Vivaldi cell array is below -28dB. The decrease in isolation, can fully show that the absorbers has a better effect of absorbing electromagnetic waves between the two antenna elements. The designed antenna can be used to verify the realization of medical near-field microwave imaging(NMI) through the use of the distance to failure (DTF) determination technique and the highlighted target signal methodology.

articleTitle: Band-notched ultra-wideband bandpass filter with broad stopband
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a microstrip ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter (BPF) with a wide stopband region from 10.6 to 30.0GHz. The proposed UWB filter consists of two rectangular stub resonators separated by one section of quarter-wavelength-long parallel coupled line that work at the UWB frequency range. In order to avoid the interference from the upstream and downstream band of around 8 GHz used in shortwave satellite communications, a stepped-impedance resonator (SIR) is coupled to the parallel-coupled line which provides a narrow stopband. The fractional bandwidth of 105% is recorded at the center frequency of 6.3 GHz and the insertion loss of 0.3 dB and return loss of 17.0 dB are achieved in the passband.

articleTitle: Visual Design of Direct Lightning Risk Assessment Based on 3D Model Discretization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper is concerned with assessing the stroke risk of the direct lighting. Due to its complex calculation and high learning cost, the leader progression model is seldom applied to risk assessment. In order to improve the practicability of the model, an automatic 3D model discretization algorithm is established to import the assessed objects into the assessment model. Furthermore, a visual design on the basis of discretization is performed.

articleTitle: Pattern Reconfigurable Metasurface Antenna Based on Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a pattern reconfigurable metasurface antenna based on characteristic mode analysis is proposed. The designed metasurface antenna is realized by a multilayer structure. Its overall size is 0.71λ0 ×0.71λ0 × 0.05λ0. A 4×4 square metasurface is placed on the top layer. The middle layer is a square patch, and the bottom layer is ground. After adding PIN diodes, the pattern can be controlled in the XOZ plane and YOZ plane relative to the normal direction of ±30º. The designed antenna is operated at 3.75 GHz with a good gain in each radiation mode.

articleTitle: Intelligent Design of Arbitrary Bandstop FSS Through Deep Learning and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Frequency selective surface (FSS) is used for electromagnetic radiation suppression due to its unique filtering characteristics. However, it still takes some experience and time to design a FSS structure with a specific stopband for actual shielding requirements. In this paper, a method based on deep learning and elite genetic algorithm is proposed, which can realize the automatic design of arbitrary bandstop FSS structure. This method only relies on a basic FSS model and some parameter scanning data to achieve the final design, reducing the need for design experience and the labor cost of repeated iterations.

articleTitle: EM Environment Adaptability Analysis of Airborne Radar Based on Complex Network Theory
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the feasibility of using complex network theory to evaluate the adaptability of airborne radar in complex electromagnetic environment (EME). The technical and tactical characteristic indexes such as false alarm probability, detection probability, sensitivity and range of action are selected as indexes, an EME adaptability evaluation model is established based on complex network theory, and several test cases of airborne radar system are given, which proved the applicability of complex network theory in the assessment of EM suitability of airborne radar.

articleTitle: Cascading Neural Network Blocks of Transistor Level Transceiver Models
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a feed-forward neural network (FNN) framework devised for cascade-able transceiver behavior modeling. Voltage waveforms after each cascading block are predicted by the proposed method and directly fed to the next block as input. Unlike conventional IBIS-AMI models, FNN models do not interact with any SPICE-like transient solver, and hence are not limited by slow convergence or convolution. Comparison of accuracy and time efficiency are drawn and compared with a commercial simulation to demonstrate the effectiveness of employing FNN in transceiver macromodeling.

articleTitle: Design of Holographic Scalar Impedance Surfaces with Controllable Polarizations
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, holographic scalar impedance surfaces with controllable polarizations are proposed. By designing the scalar surface impedance distribution of metasurface, the direction and polarization of beams can be independently controlled. The proposed low-profile, high-gain, and low-loss antennas are easy to be produced without complex feeding networks.

articleTitle: Near Magnetic Field EMI Analysis and Modeling for a MMC Submodule
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The fast switching of power electronics devices inside the submodule of modular multilevel converter (MMC) could causes severe electromagnetic interference (EMI), and the EMI current flowing in power modules and busbars excites non-negligible near-field magnetic emission. This paper analyzes the magnetic field excited by the main circuit of MMC submodule under double-pulse test with the aid of finite element (FE) simulation. The main magnetic emission sources and radiation characteristics are discussed based on the FE results and verified by near-magnetic field measurement. Also, simplified equivalent models of the laminated busbars and power modules are proposed, which can evaluate their magnetic emission quickly and accurately.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Novel Miniaturized Ultra-thin Quad-band Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Conventional metamaterial absorber (MMA) are too large to be used in miniaturized devices such as chip systems. To solve this problem, a miniature ultra-thin MMA with four absorption peaks is proposed in this paper. The proposed MMA has a thickness of only 0.2 mm and achieves 99.6%, 97.3%, 99.8% and 99.1% absorption at 12.04 GHz, 17.26 GHz, 21.04 GHz and 23.94 GHz. The paper also analyzes the influence of parameters of the proposed MMA on the absorption performance and proves that it has a certain tunability of the absorption band. By comparing with other MMA work, the MMA proposed in this paper achieves the miniaturization of the structure while ensuring the number of absorption frequency points. This advantage provides a new solution to solve the problem of difficult loading of electromagnetic shielding structures in miniaturized chip architectures.

articleTitle: Modeling of RF Interference Caused by Solid-State Drive Noise
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, modeling of RFI problem caused by a solid-state drive (SSD) in a laptop is proposed. Two noise sources (one outside and one inside a cavity) in the SSD are reconstructed as dipole moments with magnitude-only near-field scanning data. The dipole moment inside a cavity is then replaced by a Huygens' box covering four side surfaces of the cavity using a numerical simulation. The noise voltage at an RF antenna port is calculated by combining the two reconstructed noise sources with measured transfer functions. The model is successfully validated through a comparison of the calculation with measurement results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic safety evaluation of Advanced Driving Assistance System in the anechoic chamber
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: With the development of the modernization of automobiles, the pneumatic and hydraulic auxiliary mechanisms on traditional passenger cars have been basically replaced by electronic auxiliary mechanisms. This paper studies the electromagnetic radiation immunity test methods of three typical ADAS functions of vehicles. The research results have promoted the implementation of relevant standards while also integrating traditional cars. The concept of "Electromagnetic Compatibility" extends to the new field of "Electromagnetic Safety".

articleTitle: Field-to-Wire Coupling Model for Four-twisted Twisted-Wire Pairs Above Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: An approximate multiconductor transmission-line (MTL) model is obtained to characterize electromagnetic wave coupling with four-twisted twisted-wire pairs (FTWPs) running above a ground plane. The average per-unit-length (p.u.l.) parameters and equivalent coupling sources accounting for field-to-wire coupling effects for FTWPs are obtained. On the basis of p.u.l. parameters, the nonuniform MTL can be equivalent to uniform MTL with equivalent coupling sources. The proposed model is used to predict both common mode (CM) and differential mode (DM) currents induced at terminals of FTWPs and is verified by full-wave simulations with good agreement and high computational efficiency.

articleTitle: General platform designed for E3 risk assessment based on software-defined radio (SDR) principles
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this article, technical problems existing in the electromagnetic environmental effect (E3) on electronic systems are investigated, such as electromagnetic (EM) stress and effect data acquisition. Considering that the software-defined radio (SDR) has the capability of module reconfiguration, it is introduced into the electromagnetic (EM) risk assessment, and thus an experimental platform is designed based on SDR for high-power electromagnetic (HPEM) effect on wireless communication systems. The platform is composed of a multi-band RF transceiver, a baseband data processor with SDR, a monitoring EM stress subsystem and an effect database. Additionally, the potential applications of the platform in EM environment prediction, EM stress modeling, effect analysis are also illustrated.

articleTitle: Design of Conformal Snake-Shaped Line Based Dicyclic Nested Electromagnetic Bandgap Structure for SSN Suppression
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A novel conformal snake-shaped line based dicyclic nested electromagnetic bandgap (SDN-EBG) structure is proposed in this paper. The SDN-EBG is used to suppress the synchronous switching noise (SSN) in high-speed digital circuits. The EBG structure, in which the snake-shaped line is introduced on the basis of the traditional L-bridge, is conformal and has an ultra-wide stopband. For the suppression depth of -40 dB, the stopband bandwidths of planar and conformal structures are 1.7-26.7 and 1.7-24.2 GHz, respectively. It could be found that the properties of the SDN-EBG structure are not affected after conformal. In addition, the E-field distributions inside and outside the bandgap verify high impedance characteristics of the proposed EBG structure.

Author Keywords: snake-shaped line based dicyclic nested electromagnetic bandgap (SDN-EBG)

articleTitle: Research on Common Mode Voltage Characteristics of Vehicle Drive Motor System under Different Working Conditions
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The driving motor system for new energy vehicle (NEV) mostly adopts PWM technology, and its output voltage contains a large number of common mode voltage, which is one of the main EMI sources of NEV. Therefore, studying the common mode voltage characteristics of NEV driving motor system is an important means to solve the EMI problem. Due to the actual vehicle driving condition, the electric drive system has acceleration, deceleration, constant speed, heavy load, light load and other working conditions. Besides, even the path of common mode voltage has no change, the change of IGBT switching frequency and switching rate under different working conditions will also lead to the change of the common mode voltage of the electric drive system. In this paper, the characteristics of common mode voltage under different working conditions are studied to clarify the influence of working conditions on common mode voltage.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic compatibility test methods for fuel cell engine
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Using fuel cells as power sources is the essential difference between fuel cell vehicles (FCVs) and traditional vehicles. The using of DC / DC high-power converters, DC / AC converters, motors and other high-current and high-voltage equipment makes the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) research of FCVs more urgent. As the key component of FCV, the fuel cell engine’s EMC performance will directly affect the EMC performance of the whole vehicle. This paper takes the fuel cell engine as research object, gives a reconstructed method on the existing absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) to ensure the safety and orderly operation of the entire test process by analyzing its working characteristics. And then the recommended radiated emission (RE) and radiated immunity (RI) test set-up and method are given. Finally, the EMC performance of the fuel cell engine is analyzed based on RE test as a sample.

articleTitle: Grounding characteristics of shielded wire crosstalk at high frequency
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In order to prevent the coupling of external electromagnetic signals and the internal signal of the cable itself from radiating interference to the outside, substations often use shielded signal transmission lines. However, due to the structure of the shielded wire and the limitation of the shielding effect, external interference signals can be coupled to the inner conductor through the transfer impedance of the shielding layer, and induce interference signals that cannot be ignored. Therefore, the research on shielded wire has a certain meaning. For the crosstalk problem of shielded wire, this paper proposes a crosstalk prediction method based on the Implicit-wendroff finite difference time domain algorithm (FDTD). The crosstalk of shielded wires corresponding to 100 grounding points is compared on the basis of the algorithm in this paper. The results show that a suitable grounding point can effectively suppress the crosstalk of shielded wires.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on humidity sensitivity of New DC ionization
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The offset voltage and decay time performance parameters of ionizer are greatly affected by the humidity in the working environment. In this paper, the design principle of double DC ionizer with feedback regulation system is introduced, and the humidity sensitivity is studied by experiment. By setting different humidity, the offset voltage and decay time performance parameters of this ionizer are tested. The results show that the offset voltage at each point can be controlled within ±3V in the humidity range (20%~70%). Under the conditions of ultra-low humidity (8%~15%) and ultra-high humidity (80%~90%), the performance of this DC ionizer can meet the electrostatic control requirements of electrostatic protection area. When the ambient humidity exceeds 80%, the performance is greatly affected.

articleTitle: A Novel Model for Analyzing the Electric Field Susceptibility of Print Circuit Board in MMC Submodule System
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The electromagnetic environment in the high-voltage and high-current modular multilevel converter (MMC) system is quite harsh, which makes the integrated circuit (IC) on the print circuit board (PCB) vulnerable to interference and failure. Considering the characteristics of MMC's low-frequency electromagnetic interference, this research proposed a novel field-to-trace coupling model based on the power/ground plane from the perspective of the PCB. Through quantitatively analyzing the induced interference voltage, a layout scheme that could effectively reduce the sensitivity of the PCB is found. In order to verify the accuracy of the model and the effectiveness of the new layout plan, an intuitive experiment was designed for verification. The experimental results have validated the proposed method’s effect.

articleTitle: Relations Between the Planar Region, Transition Region, and Spherical Region in the Moon excited by a Vertical Magnetic Dipole
