In this SIE, the whole target is divided into several different sub-regions by using the idea of domain decomposition (DD). Then, on the basis of the current coefficient matrix obtained by MoM, this SIE method can calculate the contribution value generated by electromagnetic flows on each component region from the sub-region by marking and partitioning the target. Moreover, two technologies are further adopted to enhance the efficiency and flexibility of this SIE method. One is that curved triangular elements and higher order hierarchical vector (HOHV) basis functions are applied, which can remarkably reduce the unknown amount of the conventional SIE. The other is that a DD method is adopted to employ a discontinuous Galerkin (DG) approach to glue conformal/ nonconformal surface grids between adjacent subdomains. It is obvious that this HO-SIE based on DDM can further increase the flexibility of geometrical modeling and accelerate the convergence of the HO-SIE for electrically large and multiscale metallic targets. Finally, two numerical results are given to demonstrate the validity of this method.

Author Keywords: higher order hierarchical vector (HOHV) basis functions

articleTitle: A Wideband Single-Cell Unidirectional Absorption Common-Mode Filter with Pattern Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A new configuration for common-mode (CM) noise absorption and suppression is proposed in a two-layer printed circuit board. By directing CM noise to a resistor, that can be absorbed and dissipated as heat. In measurement, broad CM noise absorption and suppression bands are achieved from 2.19 – 3.02 GHz and 1.78 – 3.11 GHz, respectively. Most of all, an ultra-compact size of 0.029 λg2 is achieved by a single-cell structure.

articleTitle: A Simple Analytical Approximation to evaluate Noise Levels and Maximum Coupling Frequencies During DPI Simulations on BMS IC
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Many works make use of high frequency battery models and Printed Circuit Board (PCB) models for EMC emission characterization. This work proposes those models in addition to a Battery Management System (BMS) impedance to show the effect on the noise received by the BMS under Direct Power Injection (DPI) simulations with different external components configurations. Furthermore, in order to ease some of the first design stages of the BMS and its external components, a straightforward analytical model to estimate the noise levels and its maximum coupling frequencies during DPI simulations is also elaborated and validated by simulations.

articleTitle: Circuit analysis of common mode current in coupling coils for HF broadband communication system
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper investigates common mode generation in a wideband communication system using magnetic field coupling with two coils. Two coils are placed in parallel and communicate without resonance in the frequency band below 100 MHz. In this case, the common mode current to the feeder line may cause the transmission of electromagnetic field beyond the designed communication range. The circuit analysis shows that both magnetic and electric field coupling contribute to the common mode generation. It was also suggested that the phase difference between these couplings may cancel the common mode generation.

articleTitle: Increasing Peak Power of Short Pulse Source Based on Time Reversal Focusing Cavity
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Restricted by the limited performance of electronic devices, the high-power pulse source system based on the scheme of stretching and compressing a single pulse exhibits some limits in increasing the peak power of the pulse. Time reversal (TR) technology is an adaptive synchronous focusing technique, showing a powerful capability of enhancing the peak power of the pulse by focusing amounts of multipath pulses synchronously. Based on the TR technique, we discuss the use of some enclosed metal TR focusing cavity with built-in scatterers to increase the peak power of the short-time pulses and the possibility of breaking through the limitations of the conventional pulse power source. First, we present the underlying mechanisms of generating a high-power pulse source with the traditional pulse stretching and compressing scheme, the conventional TR method, and the 1-bit TR technique. After that, to achieve the highest peak power, we designed three TR focusing cavities of built-in scatterers and numerically compared their performances using the conventional TR technique and the 1-bit TR technique. The results show that the rectangular TR focusing cavity with a built-in oblique tangential scatterer together with the 1-bit TR technique exhibits the capability of generating the highest peak power pulses.

articleTitle: NRZ and ENRZ SerDes System Comparison With Proposed GA Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This study compares the channel loss performance of the ENRZ high speed signaling technique against NRZ with equalization applied. A FIR CTLE linear SerDes equalization system is built up in Matlab. Genetic Algorithm is employed to locate the optimal SerDes settings with a much less time-consuming. The comparison shows that due to ENRZ algorithmic advantages, although ENRZ has a smaller eye height than NRZ when channel loss is low, its eye height exceeds that of NRZ when the channel loss goes beyond 12 dB in this study. Meanwhile, throughout the loss range, ENRZ gives a larger eye width than NRZ which is most advantageous especially with high channel loss.

articleTitle: Dispersion Analysis and Advantages of High-order Discrete Singular Convolution FDTD
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-order Discrete Singular Convolution (DSC) FDTD method. The numerical characteristics of the dispersion are studied. It can be seen that the smaller the spatial step size, the smaller the dispersion error, and the higher-order scheme has a lower numerical dispersion error. Even the dispersion error under the coarse grid is very close to the dispersion error of the traditional central difference under the fine grid. And examples show that the high-order DSC-FDTD method is useful and valuable as a time-domain high-order method.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Conformal Symplectic FIT Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Based on Open CASCADE Object Libraries, an open-source library for Computer Aided Geometry Design (CAGD), the technique of complex geometry modeling and the conformal grid generation method in Yee grids are given. Based on the conformal grid system, the simple conformal (SC) symplectic finite integration technique (FIT) scheme is presented to advance electromagnetic fields without time step reduction.

articleTitle: A new hybrid method in the calculation of crosstalk of shielded cable
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A hybrid method is proposed by combining the field and circuit. Firstly, the circuit model is modeled through the multi-port network from the perspective of the circuit. It makes the modeling and solving process simpler and improves efficiency. Secondly, using the electric field integral equation (EFIF) and the Method of Moments (MOM) to solve the distribution parameters from the perspective of the field, makes the parameters more accurate and the bandwidth higher. Finally, compared with the experimental values, it is verified that the proposed method has good accuracy.

articleTitle: Study on comprehensive test of electrostatic properties of graphene coating
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the electrostatic performance of graphene coating samples is comprehensively evaluated and tested, focusing on the resistance (volume resistance and surface resistance) and electrostatic dissipation characteristics of the coating, and the differences of electrostatic performance of coatings with different graphene addition are investigated; The changes of electrostatic properties of graphene coating were studied by simulating vacuum, alternating high and low temperature, UV-vis and other environments. It is found that the content of graphene has a significant effection on the resistance and electrostatic dissipation characteristics of the samples. The higher the content of graphene, the lower the resistance and the shorter the electrostatic decay time; Vacuum, high and low temperature alternating environment have little effection on the electrostatic performance of graphene coating, but UV-Vis radiation has influence on them.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of HEMP Coupling Effect on Motor Drive System for Special Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: High-altitude electromagnetic pulses (HEMP) pose a great threat to motor-driven special vehicles, which can cause vehicles to lose maneuverability. In this paper, based on the field-line coupling principle, the vehicle cabin and motor drive system cable models are established using CST software. The induced currents and voltages on various cables of the motor drive system and the electromagnetic responses in the cabin and on the cabin surface under HEMP irradiation are obtained by simulation. The results show that unshielded cables are coupled to high voltage and current; the installation position of the resolver at the motor shaft end and the low-voltage port of the motor controller induce a strong electric field; the intensity of the electric field coupled to the vicinity of components with metal shells is relatively large and the surface current density coupled to the area with a smaller radius of curvature and the edge of the body structure is high. Therefore, these positions need to be designed for electromagnetic protection.

articleTitle: A Set of Mono-Cone Calibration System Loaded by Resistors in Arc-Style Routes
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Resistor loading is an effective method to overcome the low-frequency reflection caused by finite length of a mono-cone calibration system. A kind of arc-style loading route is proposed and studied in this paper to suppress the influence of introducing wires. The wire radius and the resistor location are optimized to improve the frequency performance of the system. As a result, the flatness of the transfer function at the test point in the optimized system is below 3.08 dB in 0 ~ 4 GHz.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experimental Investigation on Space-Particle Trapping Efficiency of Discharge Plasma and Electrostatic Field
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In view of the threats of space-particles in space environment entering the space station during astronauts’ extra vehicular activity on orbit, a method of charging space-particle through plasma environment and trapping it by electrostatic field is studied. The charging mechanism and trapping mechanism of space-particle are analyzed. Deutsch trapping efficiency model is introduced to simulate and design the key structural parameters and excitation voltage, which affect the trapping efficiency of Electrostatic Field Precipitator (EFP). The parameter design of EFP module is determined, and the trapping efficiency of EFP module is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: A Comparison and Analyzation of IEC CISPR 36-2020/AMD1 and GB/T 18387-2017 Standards
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In order to fully understand the technical, differences between Chinese and international standards, this paper compares the contents of GB/T 18387-2017 and IEC CISPR 36-2020AMD1, analyzes the standard differences from the application scope, test limits, test requirements, test methods and result judgment, and selects vehicles to test according to the above standards. For some frequency bands, the peak value of magnetic field tested in GB/T 18387-2017 is slightly higher than that in IEC CISPR 36-2020/AMD1, which indicates that the difference of standard content will cause the difference of test results, and then may affect the standard compliance judgment results.

articleTitle: An Experiment Verification: the ESD Protection by DC Grounded Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In practical engineering, we found that the DC grounded antenna can improve electrostatic discharge (ESD) immunity. For sensitive devices or circuits related to antenna, ESD protection by antenna design is simpler, more efficient and cost effective than common measures. In this paper, the ESD protection effectiveness of using DC grounded antenna is studied. By designing the DC Grounded GPS receiving antenna, the ESD protection efficiency of its RF front-end circuits is verified. The results provide a reference for future study of ESD protection.

articleTitle: Decoupling Capacitor Placement for Flat PDN Impedance with Rogue Wave Consideration
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Target impedance has been used to guarantee the performance of the power delivery network (PDN) for many years, but it assumes the PDN impedance profile is flat without resonant peaks. However, the PDN impedance profile is never flat, so that the step response of the PDN can comprise components of multiple resonant frequencies with corresponding impedance peaks in the frequency domain. The superposition of resonant voltage waveforms excited by transitions of current load can result in worst-case scenario and then violates maximum specified voltage. A strategy of placing decoupling capacitor to flat the PDN impedance is proposed in this paper. The defined impedance deviation of the PDN impedance with the proposed method is 7.93 percent which is about two times better than 16.25 percent with commercial tools.

articleTitle: Global Sensitivity Analysis for Crosstalk of Three-Conductor Transmission Line using Sobol ′ Method
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents the global sensitivity analysis of cable crosstalk against uncertainty of parameters using the Sobol' method. The impact of these uncertain parameters is ranked based on the Sobol' indices. The result shows that the Sobol' method is feasible for global sensitivity analysis of three-conductor transmission line crosstalk model.

articleTitle: Analyzing the influence of parasitic effects on memristor STDP with the PEEC method
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Memristors have great application potential in neuromorphic chips due to their integrated functionality of storage and computing. Research on the signal integrity of memristor crossbars under the excitation of bionic spiking signals is in urgent need to promote the rapid development of neuromorphic chip industry. This paper applies the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) method to analyze the influence of parasitic effects on the spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) learning behavior of a memristor under the excitation of bionic spiking signal pairs. Study shows appreciable differences in the STDP behaviors under extremely narrow spiking signal excitations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Near-Field to 3-Meter Field Transformation based on Equivalent Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an electromagnetic reactive near-field to 3-meter field transform method based on the equivalent dipoles is proposed. Firstly, by using the near-field scanning, the real radiation source is equivalent to a dipole array. The dipoles’ positions and moments are optimized by a differential evolution algorithm. Next, the equivalent dipole array is used to predict the 3-meter field of the real radiation source. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by both the simulation and measurement results.

articleTitle: Enhanced Transmission Model for Predicting Coupling Between Electromagnetic Field and a Twisted-Wire Pair of Complex Dielectric Coatings
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an enhanced electromagnetic field coupling to twisted wire pair (TWP) model is developed and applied for predicting the terminal voltage/current responses. In contrast to the classic transmission line (TL) model, the proposed approach takes account the perturbation effect on external field due to the presence of coatings by assigning a weight (coating coefficient C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>) to the source terms contributed by transversal field component. The case study shows a significant improvement of the modeling accuracy with respect to classic TL model.

articleTitle: Regulation of Forbidden Frequency Band for Noise Isolation in PDN Using Rectangular Dielectric EBG Units
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Dielectric EBG structure is an effective method to suppress the noise coupling in power distribution network (PDN) of multilayer printed circuit board (PCB). The usual dielectric EBG structure is formed by embedding high permittivity rods with circular or square cross-section shape into the substrate of PCB. Several discontinuous band gaps can be obtained within a certain frequency range, while wide and continuous forbidden frequency band is preferred. In this paper, a method of expand the bandwidth of noise isolation using rectangular EBG units is provided. To simplify the problem under consideration, the center distance and dielectric constant of EBG unit is held constant, only the size of rectangular EBG unit is varied. In the first case, either the length or the width of the rectangular is changed. In the second case, both the length and width of the rectangular are varied, while its area is kept constant. The calculated results show that by adjusting the aspect ratio of the rectangular EBG unit, two adjacent band gaps can be merged together, therefore, the width of a single band gap can be expanded significantly, and the continuous bandwidth with noise isolation degree better than -35 dB reaches up to 5.7 GHz within 15 GHz.

articleTitle: Modeling of Airborne Ultrashort Wave Radio Receiver and Analysis of Lightning Interference Effect
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Ultrashort wave radio receiver is an important part of airborne communication equipment, which may be affected by lightning during flight. Therefore, it’s necessary to analyze the electromagnetic characteristics and its performance under lightning interference of radio receiver. In this paper, we build the behavior model of ultrashort wave radio receiver system, then we analyze both electromagnetic characteristics in normal working condition and performance degradation under lightning interference. Through results we find that the sensitivity of the receiver deteriorates rapidly and the performance deteriorates seriously in the lightning environment. This work can provide ideas for the analysis of ultrashort wave radio and the design of lightning protection.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Modeling for Capacitance Determination of Resonant Reactive Magnetic Shield in Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: An equivalent circuit model (ECM) for capacitance determination of resonant reactive shielding (RRS) coil in magnetic resonant wireless power transfer (MR-WPT) system is proposed in this paper. The magnetic coupling between RRS coil and the transmitting (Tx) coil of a MR-WPT system is analyzed using the proposed ECM. The relationship between the compensative capacitance of RRS coil and the resonant capacitance of Tx coil is deduced and validated using full wave simulation.

articleTitle: Influence of Conformal Coatings on the EMC Performance of a Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Conformal coatings are often applied to printed circuit boards to protect the board and its components from environmental factors like moisture, chemicals, and vibration. The impact of a conformal coating on crosstalk and radiated emissions was studied in the following paper. Two coating materials were characterized in terms of their permittivity and permeability. The impact of the conformal coating was evaluated based on the crosstalk between microstrip traces, the radiated emissions from a switch-mode power supply (SMPS), and on coupling from an EMI filter to nearby components. The coatings increased crosstalk between microstrip traces by up to 5 ~ 6 dB, and increased radiated emissions from the SMPS by up to 8 dB. While the coating did not affect the performance of the EMI filter, a 5.5 dB increase in coupling was observed from the filter to nearby components. These effects should be considered if pre-compliance testing is performed before the coatings are applied.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Model of Strip Line up to 110GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Based on the wafer level packaging technology, different widths and lengths of the strip line was designed, fabricate and measured. Meanwhile, to characterize the high frequency characteristics of the strip line, the skin effect has been considered to the transmission line theory equivalent circuit model. The proposed model is in good agreement with the measured data of the strip line in the frequency range of 10 GHz – 110 GHz. The proposed model can effectively support the co-simulation of the active device model and passive device model in heterogeneous integrated package, accelerate the optimization speed of circuit design iteration, and help reduce the time cost of the EM simulation of layout.

articleTitle: A Neural Network Model for Electro-thermal Effect Affected Hot Carrier Injection Reliability in N-Type Nanoscale MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Hot carrier injection (HCI) is a detrimental phenomenon and affects device reliability in circuit. In this paper, electro-thermal effects in nanoscale field effect transistor are simulated numerically, and the transient temperature response of the device is obtained. Furthermore, based on the transient temperature response to different stress voltages, HCI-induced threshold voltage shift (TVS) is captured numerically, and it agrees well with others’ measured results. An artificial neural network (ANN) is then developed as an empirical model to reduce simulation cost. The model is trained by numerical simulation data. It has a good performance in predicting TVS, and greatly reduces the time required for numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Wideband and High Gain Fabry-Pérot Antenna Array with High-Isolation
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A wideband and high gain Fabry-Pérot (F-P) antenna array with high isolation is proposed for 5G applications. Dual polarization patch antenna is used as feed antenna. The proposed partially reflective surface (PRS) consisted of square rings and irregular radiative patches is used in wideband FPRA, and the units cell obtains a positive phase gradient in the frequency of 24–29 GHz. Metamaterial absorbers are used to improve the isolation between the two antenna elements, its absorptivity is greater than 85% over the entire operating band for TE and TM waves at incident angles of 0° to 40°. Simulated results show that the impedance bandwidth ranges is from 22.7 to 28.5 GHz (22.6% FBW), and the realized gain is up to 12.2 dBi. A decoupling absorbers could achieve over 21.5-dB isolation improved. It can be used in wearable devices for human health detection.

articleTitle: Simulation Design and Optimization of Multi-Channel High-Frequency Transmission Lines Applied to Optical Modules
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Throughout this paper, the signal integrity (SI) problem of the high-frequency signal transmission of the electro absorption modulator (EAM) array chip has been solved, which is caused by crosstalk and signal reflection in the multi-transmission line. An eight-channel high-frequency transmission line structure is proposed and optimized through electromagnetic simulation. We proposed four structure that might improve the signal integrity, that is covering ground, siding metallization, grounding hole and all above at the same time. The simulation result shows that only covering ground and doing three methods at the same time can improve the signal integrity. The original model is processed with covering ground, the -3 dB bandwidth exceed 50 GHz, and the crosstalk between adjacent lines below -25 dB. Therefore, the Multi-channel transmission line we proposed could be applied to 800 G and 1.6 T EAM array chip.

articleTitle: Common Mode Far-field Radiation Prediction of V-shaped Cables Based on Retarded Partial Element Equivalent Circuit Method
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: It is well known that the common mode (CM) current accounts for the main reasons of the far-field radiated electromagnetic noise of power cables. Therefore, this paper studies the far-field CM radiation prediction from a V-shaped power cables, which is based on the retarded partial element equivalent circuit (τPEEC) method. In this paper, the circuit matrix model and radiation formulas of τPEEC method are firstly introduced, then the planar V-shaped flat cables are modeled using this method. The radiation results predicted by this τPEEC method are compared with the simulated results and the measured results in anechoic chamber. These results verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Optimization Approach for Predicting Worst-Case Positions in EMI Final Measurement Based on Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we present an improvement in existing Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) measurement according to the norm FCC§ 15.209 in the range 30MHz to 1GHz. A developed measurement tool and a convolution neural network(CNN) were used to reduce the required time to carry out the final measurement on critical frequencies by predicting the radiation emission and then determining the position azimuth of the turntable and the height of the antenna that meet the maximum radiated emission level. The neural network was trained using real EMI measurements which were performed in the Semi Anechoic Chamber(SAC) by Cetecom GmbH in Essen, Germany.

articleTitle: Study on electromagnetic characteristics of planar inductors being of weak electromagnetic radiation interference
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Inductor is one of the important parts of switching power supply. Planar inductors have the advantages of small volume, low loss, small magnetic flux leakage, good thermal characteristics and electromagnetic compatibility, which can achieve high efficiency and high power density of high-frequency switching power supply. The extraction of inductor parameters is of great help to the design of inductors, the simulation of converters and the research of electromagnetic interference. In this paper, the analytical model and the calculation of the lumped parameters of planar inductors with magnetic core are discussed. A 3D finite element model is established to extract the parameters of the planar inductor by ANSYS software. Finally, analytical calculations, simulations and experimental measurements are carried out on a designed planar inductor, which verifies the accuracy of the 3D FEA.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of System-level Power Integrity and Signal Integrity of Vehicle Chip DDR
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In an automobile chip SoC system, due to the characteristics of high signal density and fast read-write speed, DDR system will face the problems of signal integrity such as reflection, crosstalk and insufficient timing. These problems are the key to the success or failure of the whole DDR system design. Therefore, it is necessary to carry out system level pisi simulation of DDR to verify the quality of its signal before streaming. Based on this requirement, a system level pisi simulation method for DDR is proposed in this paper. Based on IBIS Plus model, the simulation topology is constructed, and the burst frequency mode is used for simulation verification. The results are summarized and analyzed, which provides a direction for designers to solve power integrity and signal integrity problems.

articleTitle: A Novel Angularly Stable Wide Passband Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A novel wide passband frequency selective surface (FSS) design operating at 15 GHz with a -3dB bandwidth of 5.6 GHz is proposed in this study. As the proposed FSS design is symmetric structure, it shows good angle stability characteristic under different EM incident angles. The equivalent circuit is provided to explain the working principle of the design. The proposed FSS design is a good candidate for radome.

articleTitle: Design of UWB Microstrip Antenna Based on A New Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new optimization algorithm, which combines the different structures of genetic algorithm(GA) and particle swarm optimization(PSO), solving the disadvantages of a single algorithm. This paper proposes two new methods of automatic design: "Automatic search" on the patch for cutting(ASC) and creating "Defected Ground Structure"(DGS) with the proposed algorithm. The experimental results show that the S11 parameters of the antenna can meet the requirements of -10dB in the UWB frequency band of 3.1-10.6GHz. In addition, the performance of the antenna can be achieved in the wider band of 2.5-20GHz, which further expands the frequency band of the UWB antenna.

articleTitle: A Novel Circuit Modeling Approach for Electromagnetic "Black-box" Problems based on Generative Adversarial Networks and Partial Element Equivalent Circuit Method
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Reconstructing the electromagnetic properties of an unknown electronic component with limited or little information is challenging. In this paper, a new circuit modeling approach for a component in a "black-box" is proposed by tackling nonlinear inverse scattering problems (ISPs). A pixel-to-pixel generative adversarial network (pix2pix GAN) is built to infer the conductor structures within a space of interest from the measured electric/magnetic fields in a near-field region. The circuit model of the component is subsequently generated by the partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) method based on the derived conductor structures. The proposed pix2pix GAN is developed and optimized according to computational electromagnetics principles and numerical experiment. Learning from a tailored training set that imitates the conducting traces of integrated circuit, the pix2pix GAN confines the solutions to a physically meaningful subset. The proof-of-concept example shows that a well-trained pix2pix GAN can effectively reconstruct conductor structures with high confidence and have excellent agreement with the ground truth.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Energy Harvesting Technology for Smart Grid Application
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The electromagnetic energy harvesting technology is a new and effective way to supply power to the condition monitoring sensors installed on or near the transmission line. We will use Computer Simulation Technology Software to simulate the different designs of stand-alone electromagnetic energy harvesters The power generated by energy harvesters of different design structures is compared and analyzed through simulation and experimental results. We then propose an improved design of energy harvester.

articleTitle: The Influence of Ethernet Transformer Connection Method on System Common-Mode Radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: With the popularity of Ethernet, unshielded twisted pair (UTP) cables are widely used for data transmission. The common-mode (CM) noise generated in the printed circuit board (PCB) circuit is easily radiated into the space through the UTP cable, causing radiation interference. At the Ethernet port, it is the most effective and feasible way to suppress the noise entering the UTP cable from the PCB. This article takes the conventional voltage-driven PHY network port circuit as the research object. Through the analysis of the common-mode choke (CMC) and the center-tapped transformer inside the Ethernet transformer, the connection method of the Ethernet transformer is changed to achieve the optimal suppression of the CM current. This research further optimizes the filtering performance of the network port circuit without adding additional circuit components and ensuring the stable operation of the system, which has a good reference significance for the design of the Ethernet network port circuit.

articleTitle: Low infrared and optically transparent mobile phone signal jammer for Sub-6 GHz 5G band
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A low infrared and optically transparent mobile phone signal jammer based on metamaterial for Sub-6 GHz frequency band of 5G was proposed in this work. It is a multilayer structure which consisting of a low-infrared emission layer of a periodic indium tin oxide (ITO) patch array attached to an optically transparent polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film, two polyvinyl chloride (PVC) compensation layers and a microwave absorption layer of patterned ITO etched on the PET. The shielding effectiveness (SE) of the proposed signal jammer reaches above 28dB from 3.3 to 5 GHz. It also holds great performance in wide angle, conformal and optically transparent for signal shielding of Sub-6 frequency band of 5G.

articleTitle: A Fast and Accurate Rational Fitting Model for Sommerfeld Integrals in Multilayered Planar Medium
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a fast evaluation technique for the spatial domain Green’s function in multilayered planar media via rational fitting. Different from the previous approaches first fitting the spectral domain Green’s function, the proposed method performs the fitting procedure purely in the spatial domain, hence the fitting accuracy is controllable. To minimize the number of samples evaluated by time-consuming numerical integration, an adaptive fitting procedure is designed. The superior performance of the proposed method compared with the conventional closed-form approximation method is verified through numerical studies.

articleTitle: Predict and Eliminate EMI Signals for RF Shielding-Free MRI via Simultaneous Sensing and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: All clinical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners require bulky and enclosed RF shielding rooms to prevent external electromagnetic interference (EMI) signals during data acquisition, and quality electronics inside shielding room (i.e., with minimal EMI emission). A novel strategy of simultaneous EMI sensing and deep learning is presented to model, predict and remove EMI signals from acquired MRI signals, completely eliminating the need for RF shielding. We demonstrated that this method worked robustly for various EMI sources from both external environments and internal scanner electronics, producing final image SNRs highly comparable to those obtained using a fully enclosed RF shielding cage in 0.055 Tesla and 1.5 Tesla MRI experiments.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Microwave Limiter by Using T-Type LC Network Topology with GaAs Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A miniaturized ultra-wideband microwave limiter with low insertion loss is presented in this paper. This limiter adopts a three-stage antiparallel diode structure. A T-type LC network topology consisting of two spiral inductors and a parallel grounded metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitor is utilized to replace the traditional λ/4 transmission line in series between the limiting circuits. Compared with the traditional topology, the proposed limiter has the advantages of miniaturization and ultra-wideband. The area of the presented microwave limiter chip is only 1.25×0.75mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The simulation results show that the limiter can work in 0.05-18GHz. Insertion loss is less than 0.65dB at 18GHz. The output power can be maintained below 15dBm with a maximum power input of 40dBm continuous wave.

articleTitle: Broadband Electromagnetic Compatibility Model of Three Phase Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In the working process of electric drive system, the switching characteristics of motor controller produce broadband and high amplitude electromagnetic interference (EMI), which poses a threat to itself and other electronic and electrical equipment. In this paper, an innovative modeling method for three phase synchronous motor is introduced, which considers broadband parasitic effect. Based on this method, an equivalent model of a 140kW permanent magnet synchronous motor is constructed, and the accuracy of the model is verified by comparison with practical test. With wide frequency range, good convergence and high accuracy, this method can be cascaded with other electronic and electrical modules to form a complete electric drive system model, which can effectively support the rapid analysis and prediction of system level EMI and electromagnetic susceptibility (EMS) problem.

articleTitle: A Wideband Balanced-to-Unbalanced Power Divider Based On Coupled Lines
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel wideband balanced-to-unbalanced (BTU) power divider with phase inverter. Two cascaded T-shaped sections are applied in the design to realize the phase inverter, which reduces the electrical length of transmission lines (TLS). The traditional even/odd-mode analysis methods are employed to obtain the closed-form analytical equations. This circuit shows good performance in differential-mode (DM) respond, common-mode (CM) suppression and isolation. To verify the correctness of the proposed concept, a practical power divider with 4-dB differential-mode bandwidth fractional of 61.8% is designed.

articleTitle: Improved Current Clamp Voltage Level Setting Procedure in Conducted Immunity Tests
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an improved current clamp voltage level setting procedure for conducted immunity testing is presented. The analysis shows that the use of measured factors instead of theoretical 15.6 dB factor in the procedure can help to reduce the effect caused by level setting setup differences. This will better ensure adequate test results repeatability at different facilities. Furthermore, the sensor level fluctuation using the reference parameter obtained from the measured factor is smaller than that using the reference parameter obtained by the 15.6 dB factor.

articleTitle: Research on the Electromagnetic Environment of the Airborne VLF DTWA
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Airborne very low frequency (VLF) radio has great transmitting power and the ability for long distance communication, however, the HPEM field generated by airborne VLF antenna has a great threaten to the airborne equipment and personnel. Due to the irregular configuration of the antenna and the fuselage as a part of the antenna, the electromagnetic environment in the aircraft is very complex. In this paper, the electromagnetic environment of the airborne dual trailing wire antenna (DTWA) is simulated. The EM field and the surface current of the aircraft is calculated and the effect of the fuselage apertures is analyzed. The conclusions are helpful for the further research on the application of airborne VLF communication system.

articleTitle: Failure Detection and Identification of UAV Positioning System Based on Equivalent Dynamic Test Method
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The positioning system is an electromagnetically sensitive weak unit in the UAV system, and its immunity limits the performance of UAV in complex electromagnetic environment. In order to effectively improve the reliability of UAV positioning system, this paper designs the equivalent dynamic test system to carry out the radiation interference effect experiment in the microwave anechoic chamber. The sensitive frequency ranges of UAV positioning system are summarized, and the failure types are identified and analyzed. The experimental results show that radio frequency interference (RFI) induces two different failures to the positioning system. The frequency of RFI from 30MHz to 1GH causes the positioning system to temporarily stop working, and the failure will recover automatically after the interference frequency changes. The frequency of RFI from 1GHz to 3GHz affects the demodulation of GPS signal, and the positioning system cannot work normally in the whole frequency range. This phenomenon shows that the coupling paths of RFI in different frequency ranges into UAV positioning system are different.

articleTitle: An Improved Differential Evolution Optimization-Based Source Reconstruction Method by Employing Near-field Scanning
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: An improved source reconstruction method (SRM) based on near-field (NF) scanning is proposed in this paper. The differential evolution (DE) optimization method is employed to calculate the equivalent dipole model, which is used as reconstructed source. Compared with the conventional SRM, in order to achieve faster convergence, magnetic dipoles in the x, y directions and electric dipoles in the z direction are optimized concurrently according to magnetic NF data in the x, y directions and electric NF data in the z direction respectively at the beginning of the iteration. In addition, electromagnetic dipole and NF data in the x, y and z directions can be arbitrarily selected to improve the effectiveness and flexibility. The accuracy of the NF pattern on the validation plane, predicted coupling power of victim microstrip line and predicted 3-meter far field can verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Electrification modeling method for the cable network of electronic system
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: To transform the structural model of electronic system cable networks into an electrification model that can be used for electromagnetic simulation, a layered structure modeling method based on the connection table is proposed. This method divides a cable network into five levels: cable harness, cable harness branch, cable, signal, and signal port. The electrification of each layer is definite by transforming the information in the connection table and the original structural model or adding some necessary material parameters and data. In this paper, a common connection table is used as an example. The electrification model of this cable harness is implemented in the computer-aided engineering software, and crosstalk simulation is performed. The simulation results can correctly represent the electrical characteristics of this cable harness, which shows that the proposed method is accurate, and the electrification model can be used for the electromagnetic simulation of the cable network.

articleTitle: De-Embedding for Coupled Three-Port Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In many applications, the device under test (DUT) is embedded into a test setup. Various de-embedding techniques have been proposed to expose the real electrical behaviors of a DUT, e.g., the traditional thru-reflect-line and short-open-load-thru algorithms, where the T-matrix and its inverse form are adopted in the mathematical process. In the fields of radiofrequency and electromagnetic compatibility, a DUT may have three coupled ports, and the symmetry in the associated S-matrix breaks down, because the numbers of entry and exist ports are not equal, which results in a non-square T-matrix based upon the definitions. Given that the inverse expression of a non-square matrix does not exist, the conventional de-embedding methods are not applicable for a coupled three-port network. In this paper, a de-embedding algorithm which is feasible for coupled three-port devices is proposed and verified through the measurement-based studies. The de-embedding technique may also be applied on devices with more than three ports.

articleTitle: A Novel Miniaturized Dual-band Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel frequency selective surface (FSS) structure with miniaturized, low-frequency ratio. The proposed FSS is composed by cascading a curved cross ring and a double square ring (DSL)and is centrosymmetric. It exhibits the stable performance against the variation of the incident angles from 0° to 60° for both TE and TM polarizations.

articleTitle: Peak Currents of Return Strokes Observed in the Chinese Inland Areas by Ningxia FALMA
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: We have studied the currents of return strokes (RS) observed in the Chinese inland areas by a low-frequency multi-station mapping system called Ningxia Fast Antenna Lightning Mapping Array (FALMA). The RS currents are estimated through the peak-to-current conversion coefficients which are based the time-matching with a modest number of RS from the calibrated lightning location system. The statistical results show that the arithmetic means of positive and negative RS currents are 31.5 and 22.8 kA, respectively. In our dataset, the positive RS with currents below 10 kA is up to 27% indicating that small positive discharge pulses should be taken into account seriously. Overall speaking, compared to the previously reported results, the RS in the Chinese inland areas tend to show some significant differences. We will further study the possible reasons for attributing to such differences in the future.

articleTitle: Efficient Uncertainty Quantification of Stripline Pulse Response using Singular Value Decomposition and Delay Extraction
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the use of data post-processing methods with stochastic collocation, an efficient alternative to Monte Carlo sampling, for transient response parametrization in electronic design. This method is applied to find the statistics of the broadband voltage response of a 50Ω terminated stripline with uncertain width, length, and per-mittivity. Collocation results with post-processing are compared against that of Monte Carlo showing greater accuracy for a low computational budget.

articleTitle: Secondary Electron Emission Characteristics of Tantalum
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Multipactor caused by the secondary electron emission phenomenon, has been a bottle neck problem for high-power satellite components. In this paper we report a metal material with low secondary electron emission yield, tantalum. The secondary electron emission yield of tantalum was calculated by Casino when the electron beam is perpendicularly incident on a smooth tantalum surface. Moreover, the low secondary electron emission characteristic of tantalum was preliminarily verified by contrast analysis of gold and silver. The multipactor thresholds of the Ku-band impedance transformers of silver and tantalum are analyzed and compared by CST. The simulation results further validated the application possibility of tantalum in microwave components and its advantages in the field of multipactor suppression.

articleTitle: Common-Mode Noise Mitigation Method for Planar Transformer Based on FB LLC converter
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Planar transformers (PTs) have attracted tremendous attentions in many applications requiring low-profile power converters, such as server center and telecom. Today, traditional PTs still face large common-mode (CM) noise due to inter-winding capacitances and lager winding losses due to large eddy current in solid windings. Previous works show that there may exist a compromise between AC winding losses reduction and CM noise reduction. The paper proposes a novel high-performance PT based on CM currents cancellation in full-bridge (FB) LLC resonant converter and a novel winding arrangement to achieve low CM noise and low AC losses in PT. A 1.5kW 400V/50V FB LLC resonant converter prototype has been built as a platform to verify CM noise cancellation in PT of the proposed method. Experiment results show over 20dB CM noise reduction can be achieved while keeping low AC losses.

articleTitle: Reference less Far-field Radiation Measurement System for Vehicle EMC Based on Software-Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Power converters are one of the main sources of electromagnetic interference (EMI) in the automobile industry. Fast switching of the power converter over the high frequencies will always result in severe electromagnetic interference. A low-cost testing system for measuring the EMC far-field electromagnetic radiation in this study was proposed. The approach employed here employs a low cost receiver to obtain information about the signal's amplitude and phase. A near-field to far-field transformation is then used to assess far-field radiation after the amplitude and phase have been determined. The boost-buck converter measuring results prove the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: HV-LV Coupling Attenuation Measurement Test and Data Processing of Hydrogen-Oxygen Fuel Power Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The HV-LV(high volgate and low voltage) coupling attenuation measurement test is a relatively new type of electromagnetic compatibility test, which has received more and more attention from component manufacturers and vehicle manufacturers in recent years. The hydrogen-oxygen fuel power cell is in the research and development stage, and its high and low pressure coupling path is not yet clear. At this stage, the coupling attenuation can be obtained through the HV-LV coupling attenuation measurement test, and then the interference and crosstalk between the high voltage and low voltage components of the hydrogen-oxygen fuel power cell can be obtained. This is crucial for improving the electromagnetic compatibility and safety performance of hydrogen-oxygen fuel power cells. According to GB/T 18655-2018 "Vehicles, boats and internal combustion engines-Radio disturbance characteristics-Limits and methods of measurement for the protection of onboard receivers", this paper conducts a HV-LV coupling attenuation measurement test for a certain type of hydrogen-oxygen fuel power cells, and introduces test methods and data processing methods.

articleTitle: A Platform for Properties Investigation of Narrow Gap Electrostatic Discharge
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A new measurement platform testing electrode moving speed effect on discharge parameters was designed and manufactured following analysis of problems in references and pondering thought. The novel testing platform took advanced of structure of crank link motion gear and mechanotronics. The problem hence was resolved by the new design: that electrode need to move at high speed to the target but must avoid strong collision for protecting instrument from damage—which has perplexed researchers for long time. Theoretical analysis and algorithm on electrode moving speed effect were given based on two basic theorems in fluid mechanics. The platform was employed to verify primarily result from theoretical and algorithm analysis of electrode moving speed effect. Discussion was given, at the same time, on influence of discharge result caused by variation of gas pressure.

articleTitle: A Compact and Narrow-Band Bandpass Filter Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a compact and narrow-band bandpass filter (BPF). The spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPP) waveguide structure based on 3-D silicon process can be folded in space, and its electrical size can be decreased significantly. The asymptotic frequency of the proposed structure is 71.8% lower than that of the traditional rectangular groove structure with the same geometry. A compact narrow-band BPF can be obtained by combining the proposed SSPP structure with half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW). The filter operates in the frequency range of 5.43-6.8GHz with a center frequency of 6.115 GHz, and its electrical size is 0.206λg × 0.037λg.

articleTitle: Wideband Dipole/Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: 1:3 bandwidth dipole antenna is proposed, where in fact the antenna is a monopole with a modified ground. The frequency range of the antenna is 1 to 3 GHz, matched to VSWR = 2. The directivity of the antenna is between 2 to 3 dBi and the average total efficiency is -0.3 dB. The squint is not greater than one degree. The combined structure of dipole and monopole eliminates the need of using any BALUN structure.

articleTitle: Design of S-band frequency selective surface based on multi screen structure
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, two kinds of band stop frequency selective units with S-band transmission are designed, one with X-band cut-off and the other with Ku-band cut-off. The stopband bandwidth is widened by the combination of the two elements. The frequency selective surfaces (FSS) are analysed and calculated by utilizing the spectral-domain approach. In the transmission band, the transmission coefficient in dual polarization is less than 1dB. The average transmittance of the combination unit is less than -40dB in X and Ku cut-off bands, which can provide guarantee of wide-band stealth for radar system in X-band and Ku-band.

articleTitle: A Fast Method to Simulate the Average K-factor in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: We present an efficient method to simulate the average K-factor in a reverberation chamber (RC). The proposed method is based on the duality between absorption and scattering of electromagnetic waves in an RC. By replacing the rotating stirrers with absorbers, the average K-factors can be estimated quickly. Compared with the direct simulation, the proposed method is very efficient and is 15 times faster.

articleTitle: Research On Ray Path Classification in Indoor Electromagnetic Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Indoor space is an indispensable part of the whole element scene of geospatial. The study of indoor electromagnetic environment distribution is gradually get more and more attention. Deterministic methods represented by frequency-domain ray tracing method (FD-RTM) are more and more widely used in indoor electromagnetic environment modeling and analysis. Different from analyzing the multipath effect in general, this paper proposes to classify the paths in the ray tracing method based on the image theory. The propagation paths of indoor electromagnetic wave are divided into five categories: direct path, transmission path, single-reflected path, double-reflected path and mixed path. The number of different categories of paths and their power contribution at the receiving point are quantitatively analyzed, and the difference of receiving power composition of different receiving points is studied.

articleTitle: Common Mode Interference Modeling and Measurement for Cascaded Photovoltaic Grid-Connected System Module
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Modular design and medium voltage grid connection are the mainstream of large-scale photovoltaic power generation system in recent years. Investigation of the electromagnetic interference (EMI) characters of cascaded modular photovoltaic system is the basis for the implementation of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design. This paper analyzes the coupling mechanism of common mode interference in the module units of cascaded photovoltaic grid-connected system. On this basis, a common mode coupling model of multi-winding transformer and a high-frequency common mode interference model of module unit are proposed. The measurement results on a prototype verified the proposed model.

articleTitle: Investigation on Factors Influencing Discharge Characteristics of Electrostatic Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The measurement of electrostatic sensitivity of flammable and explosive materials using an electrostatic sensor is an irreplaceable procedure for electrostatic safety and management technology. But in many cases, the discharge circuit usually develops oscillations, which change the electrostatic discharge characteristics significantly, affecting the discharge energy feed and hence the measurement accuracy. This paper develops the charge-discharge circuit of electrostatic sensor in contact discharge form by modelling. The effect of voltage, stray inductance in discharge circuit, and stray capacitance of relay switch on electrostatic discharge characteristics is investigated. It is shown that, the effect of stray inductance on discharge current is relatively week, but it will introduce oscillations to the current and also decrease the discharge energy feed when its value is high up to such as 100 μH; the stray capacitance of relay switch introduces significant oscillations to discharge current.

articleTitle: Analysis of Capacitive Clamp Effect on Power Charging Cords and Plug with EFT Transient Burst Injection
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This paper investigates the coupling effect on EFT Burst transient waveform injected via CDN and capacitive clamp described in IEC 61000-4-4 [1]. We first introduce the EFT Burst transient Generator model [2] previously established published with ANSYS Designer, and which has later been adopted into ANSYS Electronics Desktop serving for immunity effect and protection measure analysis. Even though the EFT generator model has been validated with measured waveform and met pulse specification listed in the Standard, the users of ANSYS Electronics Desktop would further like to simulate their design for immunity performance in combination of EFT generator with capacitive injection clamp as test in EMC laboratory. Therefore we investigate the capacitive coupling effect on EFT waveform which injected onto EUT, for example EV charging cables and plugs, via CDN or clamp with the model of coupling network established by utilization of ANSYS Q3D and SIwave. The coupling model also takes into account the transmission line effectivity for accuracy convergence. This study intends to provide an effective simulation model to help electronic engineers enhancing their EMS design capability.

articleTitle: A Transparent Ultra-Wide Stopband Frequency Selective Surface for Millimeter Wave Electromagnetic Shielding
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: An optically transparent ultra-wide stopband frequency selective surface (FSS) for electromagnetic shielding in millimeter wave is proposed in this paper. The proposed FSS is realized by etching distinctive patterns on non-conductive glass coated with transparent conductive indium tin oxide (ITO). Full-wave electromagnetic simulations demonstrate that the FSS can achieve electromagnetic shielding from 19 to 36.6 GHz with 20 dB shielding effectiveness and exhibit response stability to oblique incidence up to 40° under both TE and TM polarizations. Finally, a prototype is fabricated and the measured results are in good agreement with the simulation.

articleTitle: Repeatability optimization method for reverberation chamber
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Compared with other Over The Air (OTA) testing system, reverberation chamber can reduce measurement cost and improve measurement efficiency. However, in practical applications, the designed reverberation chamber is found to be less repeatable. In this paper, the test method and data processing method of the reverberation chamber are optimized, and the Huber-Kalman filter is applied to the test of the reverberation chamber. As a result, the repeatability can be optimized and the measurement accuracy of the reverberation chamber can be improved.

articleTitle: Efficiently Coating Approach for Reducing Backscattering from Cavities
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Cavities are strong scattering part in aircrafts. How to efficiently coat cavities with electromagnetic (EM) absorbing materials to reduce backscattering is a significant issue in low observable aircraft design. In this letter, a variety of cavities are analyzed by an optimized discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method based on self-dual integral equation (SDIE). The scattering characteristics for various coated cavities are studied and some useful guide for coating cavities are presented.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Coaxial Conical Transverse Electromagnetic Wave Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In order to realize sweep-frequency calibration for wide band field probes with frequency 10MHz~40GHz, a new type of standard field intensity generation device-coaxial conical transverse electromagnetic wave cell (referred to as co-conical TEM cell) is researched by Beijing Institute of Radio Metrology and Measurement. According to IEC61000-4-20 standard, the standing wave, TEM wave mode, field intensity range, field uniformity and other indicators of the co-conical TEM cell are measured. The results show that this co-conical TEM cell has good performance.

articleTitle: Side-channel Information Leakage Analysis on Functional FPGA Intellectual Properties by Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The utilization of FPGA continues to rise. Studies have suggested that digital circuits may have the risk EMI side channel leakage concerns. However, there are relatively few discussions on the concerns targeted to FPGA containing different soft-cores. This paper verifies whether EMI leakage of IPs can be distinguished when they are programmed into an FPGA. This paper uses a customized measurement platform to perform EMI analyses of different FPGA soft-core architectures. These test architectures in this paper are CPU, IO control, CLOCK, counter, and FIFO. By classifying the EMI leakages through a neural network (NN) to infer its corresponding architecture, the NN can distinguish the five kinds of EMI after NN training. It is also confirmed that FPGA does have EMI side channel leakage concerns.

articleTitle: The Research on the Harness Radiation Interference Based on Six-Parameter Lumped Model for Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In the CISPR25 standard, a 1.5m-long electric vehicle (EV) wiring harness is a vital radiated emission source for measuring the radiated emission of high-voltage (HV) components based on absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) method. Firstly, the EV harness’s electromagnetic field (EMF) distribution law in the monopole antenna radiation emission test was investigated: the harness and the antenna are only coupled utilizing the electrostatic field with a specific frequency of 150kHz-30MHz. Based on this analysis, a simplified six-parameter lumped model is proposed in this paper. On the one hand, the simulation proves that the model has sufficient accuracy in describing the harness radiation emission. On the other hand, the model has a low calculation cost and meets the needs of researchers engaged in the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design of HV components.

articleTitle: Test and Assessment for Automotive Radar Interference Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: With the rapid development of automotive radar, interference problems have attracted great attention. The qualitative and quantitative analysis of interference detection and mitigation are regarded as a pivotal research field. Association standards like "Automotive millimeter wave radar interference sensing and avoidance specification" and "Test methods for radio counter-countermeasure capability of automotive millimeter wave radar product" are released recently. Based on above two standards, interference test and assessment are described in this paper, including interference estimation, mitigation in time domain, frequency domain and time-frequency domain.

articleTitle: Optimization and Design of High-Speed Transmission Line Cables
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the layered structure of the high-speed cable is firstly analyzed, and then a 3-D model is established for the cable. After that, the accuracy of the model is verified by comparing the measured data with the simulation. Finally, due to the disturbances and deformations in the actual high-speed cable, the geometric parameters of the cable are varied. According to the standard, the high-speed cable is designed and optimized, where the optimal geometry size and position are obtained. It is found that by changing the parameters of the high-speed cable, their performance can be improved significantly.

articleTitle: Modeling method for power distribution network in the micro-system packaging
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The rapid development of through-silicon via (TSV) technology provides technical support for the realization of the micro-system packaging. The power distribution networks (PDN) at different layers are connected by TSV. The small size of the TSV bring great impact to the PDN due to its large parasitic inductance. Aimed at this point, the modeling method for the multilayered PDN connected by TSV is proposed. The TSV array and power/ground plane pair are first built, then the cascaded model is built to model the multilayered PDN. To verify the accuracy of the circuit model, its result is compared with that of HFSS. The comparison results show that: the error is less than 10% within a certain frequency range of interest.

articleTitle: EMI behavior of FPGA-IP measurement
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: This study proposes a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) electromagnetic interference (EMI) measurement platform for obtaining the EMI leakage behaviors when different modules or IPs are designed in it. We should carefully regard the EMI leakage issue as the FPGA development advances. This measurement platform can observe the EMI of the time and frequency domains of an FPGA with different intellectual property (IP) modules. We program, measure, observe, and compare the EMI behaviors of different FPGA modules and IPs herein. The measurement result shows that the greatest EMI difference is observed between the blank and PLL modules, with a value of 121 dBuV on 469 MHz.

articleTitle: A Novel Probability Density Taper Approach for Planar Array Thinning
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a new approach for the synthesis of thinned periodic planar arrays featuring a minimum sidelobe level is presented. The method is based on the probability learning iterative Fourier technique (PLIFT) with a fitness function to determine element distributions for large planar array thinning, which is denoted as FPLIFT here. Compared with the traditional methods, the PLIFT acquires a minimum sidelobe level and avoids the problem of local optimum. The fitness function is used to initialize the starting parameters of the position of the elements. Then, a probability density taper is adopted to model the element distributions across the aperture. The efficiency of the FPLIFT method was validated by a representative example of array thinning with minimum peak sidelobe level. It can be demonstrated by the simulated results that the FPLIFT inherits PLIFT advantages, and results in high efficiency in reducing the side lobes. Therefore, this proposed FPLIFT can be applied in synthesis and optimization of large-scale antenna arrays.

articleTitle: A Compact Reconfigurable Filtering Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: A compact reconfigurable filtering antenna is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of a fork-shaped radiation patch, a four-pole hairpin feeding network, a T-branch and two PIN diodes. The PIN diodes inside the feeding network can switch the operation frequency bands. By turning ON/OFF the diode D1 and D2, the antenna can work in 1.5-1.6GHz (L-band for satellite communication), 2-2.1GHz (n65 band for LTE) and 3.3-3.4GHz (indoor communication for 5G). The antenna can be used for multiple purposes.

articleTitle: Analysis on the rectification of charging conduction of an electric vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The vehicle charging system has the characteristics of high efficiency and high-power density, and its electromagnetic compatibility problems are increasingly prominent in the process of operation. In this paper, the ECE R10.05 charging conduction failure test project of an electric vehicle is taken as the research object. Through theoretical analysis and engineering experience, the prototype vehicle is rectified to meet the requirements of ECE R10.05 standard.

articleTitle: Research on key Technology of Vehicle Electromagnetic Radiation Immunity Capability Verification
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Based on the research of vehicle electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) capability validation and relevant test standards, this paper puts forward a set of vehicle radiation immunity ability verification method, which includes radiation immunity field calibration and field uniformity, stability checking, deviation analysis factors such as radiation ability verification. It fill the current vehicle EMC field radiation immunity ability verification method of blank.

articleTitle: More Complete Predictions of the Near-Field Electromagnetic Emissions Based on the Derived Equivalent Dipole Model in Time-Domain
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, based on a 3D time-domain near-field scanning system, the measured magnetic fields on a PCB surface at different sampling time points are presented to visualize the wave propagation. And the magnetic fields on the left and right prediction planes are calculated by the equivalent dipoles which are derived from the top scanning data, respectively. They are in good agreement with the simulated ones. This paper is a complement to our previous work to further illustrate the effectiveness of the equivalent dipole model to predict the near-field electromagnetic emissions from the PCB.

articleTitle: A Novel Fast Generation Method of Electromagnetic Model of Multilayer Microstrip Structure (MMS) Based on Method of Moments (MOM)
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low computational efficiency caused by the huge number of mesh and difficult control of the details in the electromagnetic calculation preprocessing of MMS, a novel fast generation method of electromagnetic model of MMS based on MOM is proposed in this paper. Through the merging and subdivision of multi-layer two-dimensional geometric structures, they are grown into volume grids, and through the classification, replication and movement of grids, the electromagnetic model of MMS is quickly generated.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of the Quad-Band Negative Group Delay Circuit Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a new low-loss quad-band microwave negative group delay circuit (NGDC) based on coupled microstrip lines is presented. The circuit is mainly composed of a transmission line coupled with three groups of symmetrically coupled microstrip lines. In order to increase the absolute value of the negative group delay (NGD) at each frequency point, Genetic Algorithm is chosen to optimize the NGDC, and the NGD result has been significantly improved. Through physical processing and testing, the experimental results are in good agreement with the simulation results, which proves the quad-band NGD characteristics of the circuit and the feasibility of GA to optimize NGDC. Experimental results show that at 6.74GHz, 7.13GHz, 9.97GHz and 11.20GHz, the negative group delay values are -3.8ns, -2.7ns, -3.8ns and -5.4ns, respectively.

articleTitle: Research for Electromagnetic Interference of Automotive Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Motors have been used in the automotive industry widely, the electromagnetic interference (EMI) problem, cause by motor systems, has become a serious trouble. In this paper, the EMI performance of an automotive motor is researched based on Simulation and test. The optimized parameters of schematic are proposed via simulation, and the reliability and accuracy of the simulation are verified by the validation test. The result shows that the product can get some improvement in the EMI test. In order to cover the problem of EMI, test result exceeded the emission limit in some frequency points, some simulation analysis performed, and the validation test, with the proposed component parameters in the actual project, performed. It is a real case of forward design with electromagnetic interference simulation, and the optimized component parameter is also available for other similar motor projects.

articleTitle: The Asymptotic Method for Multi-Conductors Excited by Multiple Plane Waves with a Lossy Ground
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: The classical transmission line (TL) theory cannot deal with TLs of electrically large height. This paper presents an asymptotic method to solve high-frequency excitations induced currents of multi-conductors with a lossy ground. Using modal transformation, the analytical expression in asymptotic region is obtained, and terminal solutions are calculated numerically. Compared with the solutions using the moment of methods (MOM), the research results validate this method effectively.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Time-Frequency Characteristics of Return Current of Subway Traction Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
