abstract: The rapid development of the subway has brought a lot of convenience to people's transportation, but the negative impact of the stray current caused by the traction current of the subway locomotive on the surrounding environment cannot be ignored. During the continuous start, acceleration, uniform speed and braking of subway locomotives, the traction load of the locomotive will change with time, and the extensive use of power electronic devices in the converters of traction substations will cause the output DC current to have harmonics. Therefore, the stray current is no longer a direct current in the full sense, but a dynamic AC and DC mixed current. In this paper, the dynamic characteristics of the traction power supply return current in the subway time domain are measured on site with time, and the harmonic components of the measured current are further analyzed. The test and analysis results can provide theoretical and data support for the dynamic simulation analysis of traction power supply stray current.

articleTitle: Overview and Progress of Risk Assessment for EMC
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Modern society is based on the electronics and electrics. The electronic systems could be interfered or even damaged by the electromagnetic (EM) environments, which might cause a severe disaster or threat to the civil lives. The EM risk is difficult to find since the EM weaknesses would be hidden in the system design and no evident symptom can be observed in the normal. The concept of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is compared in parallel with the risk assessment to build the EM risk model and answer such the questions what is and how to do the EM risk assessment. The progress of the standardization on the EM risk is introduced finally.

articleTitle: A microfluidic device based on a rectangular transmission line structure for the application of picosecond pulsed electrical fields on suspension cells
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: To study the mechanisms and characteristics of electroporation caused by ultra-short pulsed electric fields (PEF) dynamically and in real-time, it is necessary to design an exposure system with the ability of wide frequency spectrum, high peak field intensity, good field uniformity, and real-time observation. In this work, we propose a design scheme by combining the fabrication process of poly (dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) and metal construction based on rectangular transmission lines to form the microfluidic device and achieve multi-performance exposure features, which can be efficiently applied in cell experiments. When a Unipolar picosecond pulse of 280 ps duration and 7 kV amplitude is delivered to the device, the numerical simulations show that the device is well designed to deliver ultra-short PEF whose intensity can be ideally up to 60 kV/cm without distortion, and the electric field distribution in the channel filled with cell suspension medium has good uniformity.

articleTitle: Simulation and Calculation of Proximity Effect of Coils Under Fast Transients
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Proximity effect over a broad frequency range plays an important role in analyzing transients in the coils. The frequency dependent characteristic makes proximity effect a tricky problem. This paper first introduces FEM simulation to calculate the complex impedance of proximity effect and compares different axial arrangement of two conductors, shows a good agreement. In addition, different formulas are used to compare their results with FEM simulation to verify their accuracy. Kane formula and Modified formula can both get relatively accurate results. Considering the accuracy and conciseness of Modified formula, it is preferred in the analysis of transients in coils.

articleTitle: Research on Impulse Characteristics of Grounding Device under Two Consecutive Lightning Strikes
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Lightning strikes are one of the main factors that threaten the safe operation of power grids. The grounding device is a key facility that leads the lightning current discharge into the ground, and protect the equipment and personal. There are multiple discharges for most lightning strikes. This paper uses numerical simulation methods to study the impulse characteristics of the grounding device under two consecutive lightning strikes. The effect of the time interval between lightning strikes and the change in the residual resistivity of the soil discharge area during continuous discharge on the impulse characteristics of the grounding device is paid more attention to. It can be seen that when the grounding device is struck by continuous lightning, if the residual resistivity of the soil discharge area is more and more reduced, the transient potential of the grounding device will be continuously reduced. However, as long as the residual resistivity is sufficiently smaller than the original soil resistivity, the difference in the value of the residual resistivity of the soil discharge area has little effect on the impulse grounding resistance.

articleTitle: Broadband Reflection-Type Metasurface for OAM Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2022 Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (APEMC)
abstract: Generating orbital angular momentum (OAM) carried by vortex beams in a broad bandwidth is imperative for communication systems. In this paper, we proposed a low-profile and wide-band metasurface to generate high-purity vortex beams by combining the polarization converter and the resonant phase. In addition, it is applicable for Linearly Polarized (LP) incident wave and Circularly Polarized (CP) incident wave. The metasurface consisting of 10 × 10 elements is used to generate vortex beam with mode l = 1. Simulation results at 15 GHz verify the feasibility of this method, which paves a new way for generating vortex beams.
